_meta.description: Source data for plans-data.js. Derived: common20 = core9+post4+mid7; wilderness11 = internal.wilderness10 + cap40final.

wilderness10.title: Man shall not live by bread alone
wilderness10.text: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
wilderness10.speaker: Jesus — in the wilderness, tempted by the devil
wilderness10.plain: In the wilderness, provision isn't just food. It's every word from God.
wilderness10.today: What are you living by — bread alone, or His Word?
wilderness10.action: Let one verse from God's mouth feed you today. Sit with it.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, I live by every word from Your mouth. Not bread alone. Amen.

wilderness10.title: He shall give his angels charge
wilderness10.text: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.
wilderness10.speaker: The psalmist — to one who dwells in the secret place
wilderness10.plain: In the wilderness, you're not alone. Angels have charge over you.
wilderness10.today: Where do you need to remember you're kept?
wilderness10.action: Name one "way" you're walking. Pray: "Keep me in this way."
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, Your angels have charge over me. I am kept. Amen.

wilderness10.title: Trust in the LORD
wilderness10.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
wilderness10.speaker: Solomon — father to son — on the core of wisdom
wilderness10.plain: Wilderness seasons strip away your own understanding. Trust replaces it.
wilderness10.today: Where are you leaning on your own understanding instead of Him?
wilderness10.action: Acknowledge Him in one decision today. Let Him direct.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, I trust You with all my heart. Direct my paths. Amen.

wilderness10.title: Bread from heaven
wilderness10.text: Then said the LORD unto Moses, Behold, I will rain bread from heaven upon you; and the people shall go out and gather a certain rate every day; that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law, or no.
wilderness10.speaker: God to Moses — in the wilderness, before the manna
wilderness10.plain: God provided daily. Not a stockpile. Daily. That's the wilderness rhythm.
wilderness10.today: Are you gathering today's portion, or hoarding yesterday's?
wilderness10.action: Receive today's portion from God. Don't reach for tomorrow's yet.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, rain bread from heaven. I gather today's rate. Amen.

wilderness10.title: The LORD is my shepherd
wilderness10.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
wilderness10.speaker: David — the shepherd-king — who knew wilderness and green pastures
wilderness10.plain: In the wilderness, the Shepherd leads. You shall not want.
wilderness10.today: What do you want that the Shepherd hasn't provided?
wilderness10.action: Say: "I shall not want." Mean it. Rest in it.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, You are my Shepherd. I shall not want. Amen.

wilderness10.title: Wait on the LORD
wilderness10.text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
wilderness10.speaker: Isaiah — to exiles in their own wilderness
wilderness10.plain: Waiting isn't passive. It renews. Eagles, running, walking—all from waiting.
wilderness10.today: Where are you running ahead instead of waiting?
wilderness10.action: Wait on the Lord in one area today. Let Him renew your strength.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, I wait upon You. Renew my strength. Amen.

wilderness10.title: Tempted like as we are
wilderness10.text: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin.
wilderness10.speaker: The writer of Hebrews — on Jesus as our High Priest
wilderness10.plain: Jesus was tempted in the wilderness. He gets it. He's touched with your infirmities.
wilderness10.today: What temptation are you facing? He was tempted like you.
wilderness10.action: Bring your temptation to Him. He knows. He's been there.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, You were tempted like me. Touch my infirmity. Amen.

wilderness10.title: God will provide
wilderness10.text: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah-jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the LORD it shall be seen.
wilderness10.speaker: Moses recording Abraham's wilderness moment
wilderness10.plain: Jehovah-jireh. The LORD will provide. Abraham learned it on the mount.
wilderness10.today: What do you need provision for? Name it. He will be seen there.
wilderness10.action: Call your wilderness place Jehovah-jireh. "The LORD will provide."
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, in this mount, You shall be seen. Provide. Amen.

wilderness10.title: Strength of my heart
wilderness10.text: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
wilderness10.speaker: Asaph — after envy nearly broke him, before he saw God's end
wilderness10.plain: When body and heart fail, God remains the strength of your heart—and your portion.
wilderness10.today: You do not have to pretend you feel strong. He is the strength when you do not.
wilderness10.action: Say aloud: "My portion is God"—even if your flesh feels like it is failing.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, my flesh and heart fail; be the strength of my heart forever. Amen.

wilderness10.title: Grace sufficient
wilderness10.text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
wilderness10.speaker: Paul — the Lord's answer to his thorn
wilderness10.plain: Weakness is not where grace ends. It is where Christ's power rests.
wilderness10.today: Where you feel weakest, ask for His strength—not to remove the thorn first.
wilderness10.action: Write one "infirmity" you will hand to Him today without fixing it yourself.
wilderness10.prayer: Lord, Your grace is sufficient; let Your power rest on my weakness. Amen.

core9.title: Name the noise
core9.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
core9.speaker: Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount
core9.plain: Stop chasing the side things. Put God first and everything else lines up.
core9.today: What are you scrolling toward instead of Him?
core9.action: Set your phone face-down for 30 minutes and open the Word instead.
core9.prayer: Lord, put You first today. Help me stop chasing what doesn't matter. Amen.

core9.title: Guard the gate
core9.text: Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just, whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report; if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise, think on these things.
core9.speaker: Paul from prison — choosing his thoughts deliberately
core9.plain: Your mind is a gate. You decide what gets in.
core9.today: What content are you letting in that you wouldn't want God watching with you?
core9.action: Unfollow or mute one account today that pulls you away from peace.
core9.prayer: Father, guard my heart. Let me choose what gets in. Amen.

core9.title: The enemy's tactic
core9.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.
core9.speaker: Peter to scattered believers under pressure
core9.plain: Distraction isn't random. It's a strategy against you.
core9.today: Where are you most distracted? That's likely where the attack is focused.
core9.action: Name the distraction out loud. Then say: "I see you. I choose God."
core9.prayer: God, I see the distraction. I choose You. Amen.

core9.title: Renew the mind
core9.text: And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind, that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.
core9.speaker: Paul calling believers to a different standard
core9.plain: The world will shape you if you let it. Renewal is active, not passive.
core9.today: What has the world's noise told you to believe this week?
core9.action: Spend 5 minutes in Scripture before touching social media tomorrow morning.
core9.prayer: Lord, renew my mind. Don't let the world shape me. Amen.

core9.title: Stand firm
core9.text: Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
core9.speaker: Paul — a prisoner writing about spiritual warfare
core9.plain: You don't fight to win. You stand because God already won. Your job is to hold the ground.
core9.today: What ground are you giving up through distraction?
core9.action: Write down one boundary you will hold today. Keep it.
core9.prayer: God, help me stand. I hold the ground You've given. Amen.

core9.title: Eyes on the prize
core9.text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith.
core9.speaker: The writer of Hebrews to a tired church
core9.plain: Drop the weight. Stop looking sideways. Eyes on Jesus, keep running.
core9.today: What weight — habit, app, person — slows your run?
core9.action: Delete one app or break one habit that distracts you from the race.
core9.prayer: Lord, eyes on Jesus. Drop the weight. Keep running. Amen.

core9.title: The peace that guards
core9.text: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
core9.speaker: Paul — same letter, same prison, same peace
core9.plain: God's peace doesn't make sense. It just shows up and stands guard anyway.
core9.today: You've battled distraction for 7 days. Where do you feel calmer?
core9.action: Pray today: "Guard my heart and mind. Keep me focused on what matters." Then rest.
core9.prayer: Father, guard my heart and mind. Keep me focused on what matters. Amen.

core9.title: Keep thy heart
core9.text: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
core9.speaker: Solomon — father to son — on what matters most
core9.plain: Everything flows from the heart. Guard it like your life depends on it. It does.
core9.today: What is leaking out of your heart into your choices this week?
core9.action: Pause before one decision today. Ask: "Is this from a guarded heart or a leaky one?"
core9.prayer: Lord, keep my heart. Guard what flows out. Amen.

core9.title: Cast down imaginations
core9.text: Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ.
core9.speaker: Paul — defending his ministry, teaching spiritual warfare
core9.plain: Thoughts that oppose God don't get a free pass. Capture them. Bring them to Christ.
core9.today: What thought has been running loose that needs to be brought captive?
core9.action: Name one thought. Say: "I bring this to the obedience of Christ." Then release it.
core9.prayer: Lord, I bring every thought captive to You. Amen.

post4.title: Set affection above
post4.text: Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth.
post4.speaker: Paul — redirecting the Colossians' focus
post4.plain: Affection follows where you set it. Choose above.
post4.today: Where is your affection set — on things above or things on earth?
post4.action: Before opening any app today, ask: "Is this above or below?" Choose one thing above.
post4.prayer: Lord, set my affection on things above. Amen.

post4.title: No man that warreth
post4.text: No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life; that he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.
post4.speaker: Paul to Timothy — a young pastor in the fight
post4.plain: Soldiers don't get tangled in civilian affairs. You're at war. Stay untangled.
post4.today: What affair of this life has you entangled right now?
post4.action: Name one entanglement. Pray: "I lay this down. I please You, not it."
post4.prayer: Lord, I stay untangled. I please You. Amen.

post4.title: One thing is needful
post4.text: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
post4.speaker: Jesus — at Martha's house — redirecting her focus
post4.plain: Many things clamor. One thing is needful. Choose it.
post4.today: What "many things" are you troubled about that aren't the one needful thing?
post4.action: Sit with the Word for 10 minutes today. That's the good part. Choose it.
post4.prayer: Lord, I choose the one needful thing. Amen.

post4.title: Love not the world
post4.text: Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.
post4.speaker: John — to believers who knew the cost of compromise
post4.plain: You can't love the world and the Father. One will win.
post4.today: What from the world are you still loving that competes with the Father?
post4.action: Name it. Then say: "I choose the Father over this." Mean it.
post4.prayer: Father, I choose You over the world. Amen.

mid7.title: Be stedfast
mid7.text: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
mid7.speaker: Paul — after the resurrection chapter — calling for steadfastness
mid7.plain: Steadfast. Unmoveable. Your labour isn't in vain.
mid7.today: Where have you been moveable when you should have stood?
mid7.action: Pick one area. Be unmoveable there today.
mid7.prayer: Lord, I am steadfast. My labour is not in vain. Amen.

mid7.title: Walk circumspectly
mid7.text: See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
mid7.speaker: Paul — on how to walk in a dark age
mid7.plain: Redeem the time. The days are evil. Walk like you know it.
mid7.today: How did you spend your time yesterday? Redeemed or wasted?
mid7.action: Redeem one hour today. Use it for something that matters.
mid7.prayer: Lord, I redeem the time. Walk circumspectly. Amen.

mid7.title: Unite my heart
mid7.text: Teach me thy way, O LORD; I will walk in thy truth: unite my heart to fear thy name.
mid7.speaker: David — in a psalm of dependence
mid7.plain: A divided heart scatters. Ask Him to unite it.
mid7.today: Is your heart united toward God or scattered toward a hundred things?
mid7.action: Pray this verse. Then notice one way your heart is divided. Bring it to Him.
mid7.prayer: Lord, unite my heart to fear Your name. Amen.

mid7.title: Watch and be sober
mid7.text: Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.
mid7.speaker: Paul — to a church waiting for the Lord
mid7.plain: Don't sleepwalk through life. Watch. Be sober.
mid7.today: Where are you sleepwalking — numb to what matters?
mid7.action: Wake up in one area today. Pay attention. Be present.
mid7.prayer: Lord, I watch and am sober. I do not sleep. Amen.

mid7.title: Run not uncertainly
mid7.text: I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air.
mid7.speaker: Paul — on his own discipline as an athlete
mid7.plain: Run with purpose. Fight with aim. No beating the air.
mid7.today: Are you running uncertainly or with clear purpose?
mid7.action: Name the race you're in. Then run one step with intention today.
mid7.prayer: Lord, I run not uncertainly. I fight with aim. Amen.

mid7.title: Number our days
mid7.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
mid7.speaker: Moses — in a psalm about the brevity of life
mid7.plain: Numbered days make wise hearts. Don't waste them.
mid7.today: How many of your days have you applied to wisdom this month?
mid7.action: Count: how many days this week did you spend time in the Word? Add one.
mid7.prayer: Lord, teach me to number my days. Apply my heart to wisdom. Amen.

mid7.title: Abstain from lusts
mid7.text: Dearly beloved, I beseech you as strangers and pilgrims, abstain from fleshly lusts, which war against the soul.
mid7.speaker: Peter — to exiles who knew the cost of compromise
mid7.plain: Fleshly lusts war against the soul. Abstain. You're a pilgrim, not a settler.
mid7.today: What fleshly lust is warring against your soul right now?
mid7.action: Name it. Abstain from it for today. One day at a time.
mid7.prayer: Lord, I abstain. I am a pilgrim. Amen.

tail8.title: Meditate day and night
tail8.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
tail8.speaker: God to Joshua — at the start of the promised land
tail8.plain: The Word in your mouth. Day and night. That's the rhythm.
tail8.today: How often is the Word in your mouth — or only in your feed?
tail8.action: Speak one verse out loud today. Let it depart from your mouth into the air.
tail8.prayer: Lord, the Word does not depart from my mouth. Amen.

tail8.title: Commit thy works
tail8.text: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
tail8.speaker: Solomon — on the connection between commitment and clarity
tail8.plain: Commit your works. Then your thoughts get established. Order follows surrender.
tail8.today: What works have you not committed to Him?
tail8.action: Commit one thing to the Lord today — out loud. Then watch your thoughts.
tail8.prayer: Lord, I commit my works to You. Establish my thoughts. Amen.

tail8.title: Draw nigh to God
tail8.text: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
tail8.speaker: James — direct and practical
tail8.plain: Draw nigh. He draws nigh. It's a two-way move.
tail8.today: When did you last draw nigh — not out of duty, but desire?
tail8.action: Draw nigh today. One step. He meets you.
tail8.prayer: Lord, I draw nigh. Draw nigh to me. Amen.

tail8.title: Pure in heart
tail8.text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
tail8.speaker: Jesus in the Beatitudes
tail8.plain: Purity of heart isn't perfection. It's single-mindedness. The pure see God.
tail8.today: Is your heart pure — single toward Him — or divided?
tail8.action: Ask Him to purify your heart in one area today. Receive it.
tail8.prayer: Lord, purify my heart. I want to see You. Amen.

tail8.title: Fear God
tail8.text: Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.
tail8.speaker: The Preacher — after trying everything under the sun
tail8.plain: The whole duty. Fear God. Keep His commandments. Everything else is vanity.
tail8.today: Is fearing God the conclusion of your matter, or an afterthought?
tail8.action: Make fearing God the first thing today. Before the scroll. Before the task.
tail8.prayer: Lord, I fear You. I keep Your commandments. This is my duty. Amen.

tail8.title: Grace teaches
tail8.text: For the grace of God that bringeth salvation hath appeared to all men, Teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.
tail8.speaker: Paul to Titus — on what grace actually does
tail8.plain: Grace teaches. It doesn't excuse. It trains you to live soberly, righteously, godly.
tail8.today: Is grace teaching you — or are you using it as an excuse?
tail8.action: Let grace teach you one thing today. Deny one ungodly impulse.
tail8.prayer: Lord, Your grace teaches me. I live soberly, righteously, godly. Amen.

tail8.title: Iron sharpeneth iron
tail8.text: Iron sharpeneth iron; so a man sharpeneth the countenance of his friend.
tail8.speaker: Solomon — on the power of true friendship
tail8.plain: You need people who sharpen you. Not just affirm you. Sharpen.
tail8.today: Who sharpens you? Who do you sharpen?
tail8.action: Reach out to one person who sharpens you. Or become that for someone.
tail8.prayer: Lord, sharpen me through my friends. Let me sharpen others. Amen.

tail8.title: Already won
tail8.text: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
tail8.speaker: Paul after explaining the resurrection — the victory is the point
tail8.plain: You're not fighting for victory. You're fighting from it.
tail8.today: Start from victory, not toward it. The battle is already decided.
tail8.action: Face today's hardest thing from this place: "He already won this."
tail8.prayer: Thanks be to God. He already won. Amen.

cap10.title: 10 days in
cap10.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
cap10.speaker: The psalmist — after 176 verses on the Word
cap10.plain: You've walked 10 days with the Word. It's lighting your path. Keep going.
cap10.today: Where has the Word lit your path this week?
cap10.action: Write down one way Scripture has guided you. Thank Him for it.
cap10.prayer: Lord, Your word is my lamp. Thank You for 10 days. Amen.

cap14.title: 14 days strong
cap14.text: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
cap14.speaker: Paul — after the resurrection chapter — calling for steadfastness
cap14.plain: Two weeks in. Be steadfast. Unmoveable. Your labour isn't in vain.
cap14.today: You've held the line for 14 days. What has shifted?
cap14.action: Write down one way you're more steadfast than when you started. Thank Him.
cap14.prayer: Lord, I am steadfast. My labour is not in vain. Thank You for 14 days. Amen.

cap21.title: 21 days — habit formed
cap21.text: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
cap21.speaker: God to Joshua — at the start of the promised land
cap21.plain: Three weeks in. The habit is forming. Don't let the Word depart from your mouth.
cap21.today: You've built 21 days. How will you keep the Word in your mouth?
cap21.action: Commit to one way you'll continue — a time, a place, a rhythm. Write it down.
cap21.prayer: Lord, the Word does not depart from my mouth. Thank You for 21 days. Amen.

cap30deep.title: 30 days deep
cap30deep.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
cap30deep.speaker: The sons of Korah — after surviving what should have destroyed them
cap30deep.plain: Not a distant help. A very present one. Right here. Right now.
cap30deep.today: You made it 30 days. Look at the ground you've held. It's real.
cap30deep.action: Write down three ways you've cut through distraction. Offer them back to Him.
cap30deep.prayer: Lord, You are my refuge and strength. Thank You for 30 days. Amen.

cap30final.title: 30 days deep
cap30final.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
cap30final.speaker: The sons of Korah — after surviving what should have destroyed them
cap30final.plain: A full month in the Word changes you. You've built something real.
cap30final.today: Even on the hardest days, you now reach for truth first instead of noise.
cap30final.action: Look back at your first day. See how far He's carried you. Thank Him out loud. Then write one sentence: "Because of these 30 days, I now..."
cap30final.prayer: Lord, thank You for every verse, every hard day, every small win. Keep building in me what You started. Amen.

cap40final.title: 40 days complete
cap40final.text: And thou shalt remember all the way which the LORD thy God led thee these forty years in the wilderness, to humble thee, and to prove thee, to know what was in thine heart, whether thou wouldest keep his commandments, or no.
cap40final.speaker: Moses — to Israel before the promised land
cap40final.plain: Forty days in the wilderness shows what's really in your heart. You made it.
cap40final.today: The testing revealed where you're strong and where you still need Him more.
cap40final.action: Take 5 quiet minutes. Remember the hardest day in this plan. See how God showed up. Then share one lesson from these 40 days with someone—or write it down if you're not ready.
cap40final.prayer: Father, You led me through these forty days. Thank You for every provision, every test, every time You carried me when I couldn't walk. I'm Yours. Amen.

capWildernessBridge.title: 30 days — into the wilderness
capWildernessBridge.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
capWildernessBridge.speaker: The sons of Korah — after surviving what should have destroyed them
capWildernessBridge.plain: Not a distant help. A very present one. Right here. Right now.
capWildernessBridge.today: You made it 30 days. The next 10 are the wilderness stretch—trust, provision, temptation.
capWildernessBridge.action: Write down one way God has been your refuge. Carry it into the next 10 days.
capWildernessBridge.prayer: Lord, You are my refuge and strength. I enter the wilderness with You. Amen.

preCap30.title: Do not weary
preCap30.text: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
preCap30.speaker: Paul — closing his letter to churches worn down by opposition
preCap30.plain: Weariness is not failure. "Faint not" is permission to rest in Him—and keep sowing.
preCap30.today: Day 29: you are not behind. In due season you will reap if you do not give up.
preCap30.action: Name one small "well doing" you can keep today without performing for anyone.
preCap30.prayer: Lord, I am weary but I faint not in You. Sustain me to day 30. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: This pain is real
painWontQuit7.text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.
painWontQuit7.speaker: Paul — the Lord's answer to his thorn
painWontQuit7.plain: Some days the pain is so loud it drowns everything else out. You're not weak for feeling it. God doesn't always take the pain away, but He promises His grace will be enough right in the middle of it.
painWontQuit7.today: Right now, say out loud: "Lord, this hurts. I need Your grace today."
painWontQuit7.action: Write down the number 1–10 for how bad the pain is right now. Be honest.
painWontQuit7.prayer: Jesus, the pain is loud today. Your grace is supposed to be enough. Help me believe it. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: I'm still here
painWontQuit7.text: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
painWontQuit7.speaker: Jeremiah — after honest grief, remembering who God is
painWontQuit7.plain: You woke up again even when you didn't want to. That counts. Every new morning is proof God hasn't given up on you yet.
painWontQuit7.today: Thank Him for one small thing that still works today (even if it's just that you can breathe).
painWontQuit7.action: Take 3 slow breaths and say "New mercies" on each exhale.
painWontQuit7.prayer: Lord, thank You I'm still here. Your mercies are new this morning. Help me use them. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: One verse, one breath
painWontQuit7.text: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
painWontQuit7.speaker: God through Isaiah — to a weary people
painWontQuit7.plain: You don't have to conquer the whole day. Just this next breath. God is holding you up when your legs won't.
painWontQuit7.today: When the pain spikes, stop and whisper this verse — even if it's through gritted teeth.
painWontQuit7.action: Set a quiet reminder on your phone: "One verse, one breath."
painWontQuit7.prayer: Father, I'm scared and hurting. Hold me up today. I'm leaning on Your right hand. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: I'm allowed to rest
painWontQuit7.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
painWontQuit7.speaker: Jesus — inviting the worn-out
painWontQuit7.plain: Rest isn't quitting. Jesus invites tired, hurting people to come to Him. You're carrying a heavy load in your body. He sees it.
painWontQuit7.today: Lie down or elevate your legs for 10 minutes and just tell Him how tired you are.
painWontQuit7.action: Do one thing today that eases the load even a little (ice, heat, stretch, whatever helps).
painWontQuit7.prayer: Jesus, I'm heavy laden today. I'm coming to You for rest. Give me some. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: Others are hurting too
painWontQuit7.text: Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
painWontQuit7.speaker: Paul — to churches learning to carry weight together
painWontQuit7.plain: Your pain is loud, but you're not the only one fighting today. Sometimes praying for someone else gives you a moment of relief.
painWontQuit7.today: Pray for one other person who's hurting right now (even if you don't know their name).
painWontQuit7.action: Leave one short anonymous line on the prayer wall (home or message board) for someone else.
painWontQuit7.prayer: Lord, someone else is in pain today too. Ease their burden and mine. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: This won't last forever
painWontQuit7.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.
painWontQuit7.speaker: John — the vision of the new creation
painWontQuit7.plain: One day the pain ends. No more hell in your legs. No more tears. This world is broken, but it's not the end of the story.
painWontQuit7.today: Picture that day — no pain, no limping, just peace with Jesus.
painWontQuit7.action: Write down one thing you're looking forward to when the pain is gone.
painWontQuit7.prayer: Father, I'm holding on for the day You wipe every tear and every pain away. Help me endure till then. Amen.

painWontQuit7.title: I'm still fighting
painWontQuit7.text: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
painWontQuit7.speaker: Paul — at the end of his race
painWontQuit7.plain: You're still here — still showing up. That's fighting the good fight. God sees every small step you take through the hurt.
painWontQuit7.today: Look back at the last 7 days. See the small wins. Be proud of them.
painWontQuit7.action: Add this plan to your streak and tell someone (or just tell God) you finished it.
painWontQuit7.prayer: Lord, I'm still in the trench. Thank You for every day I kept going. I want to finish well. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: Hope anyway
heavyHope7.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted in me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him for the help of his countenance, and my God.
heavyHope7.speaker: The psalmist — honest with his own soul before God
heavyHope7.plain: Your soul can feel down and still be told the truth: hope in God is allowed before the feelings catch up. The story in your head is loud; His countenance is steadier.
heavyHope7.today: Name one sentence your mind keeps repeating—and answer it with this verse, even if your voice shakes.
heavyHope7.action: Write "hope in God" on paper or in notes. Glance at it once before dinner.
heavyHope7.prayer: Lord, my soul is cast down. I hope in You anyway—not because I feel it, because You are my God. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: Answer me in the morning
heavyHope7.text: Cause me to hear thy lovingkindness in the morning; for in thee do I trust: cause me to know the way wherein I should walk; for I lift up my soul unto thee.
heavyHope7.speaker: David — pressed in spirit, still reaching
heavyHope7.plain: Heavy mornings are real. This prayer asks God to break through with kindness before the day argues with you.
heavyHope7.today: Before you check a screen, whisper: "Cause me to hear Your lovingkindness."
heavyHope7.action: Open the blinds or step outside sixty seconds—let light be a small anchor.
heavyHope7.prayer: Father, morning feels thick. Let me hear Your lovingkindness. I lift my soul to You. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: Oil for heaviness
heavyHope7.text: To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that he might be glorified.
heavyHope7.speaker: Isaiah — good news for the bruised
heavyHope7.plain: Scripture names a "spirit of heaviness" without shaming you. God trades mourning for oil and praise—not on a timetable that rushes your grief.
heavyHope7.today: Where does heaviness sit—in chest, gut, thoughts? Tell Him without fixing it first.
heavyHope7.action: Hum one line of a hymn or psalm you remember—even under your breath.
heavyHope7.prayer: Lord, my spirit feels heavy. You promise oil of joy and a garment of praise—give me one honest step toward You today. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: Near the broken heart
heavyHope7.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
heavyHope7.speaker: David — after fear, after trouble
heavyHope7.plain: Brokenhearted is not too far for God. Contrite does not mean "fixed"—it means humble and honest. He draws near there.
heavyHope7.today: You do not have to polish your prayer. Try one sentence of plain truth to Him.
heavyHope7.action: Place a hand on your chest. Pray: "You are nigh." Pause five seconds.
heavyHope7.prayer: Lord, my heart is broken. Draw near. Save me in the contrite place. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: Gentle and lowly
heavyHope7.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
heavyHope7.speaker: Jesus — to the worn-out
heavyHope7.plain: Heavy laden includes heavy thinking. His yoke is not another performance—it is learning from Someone meek who does not crush you.
heavyHope7.today: What burden are you carrying alone that you could name to Jesus in one sentence?
heavyHope7.action: Sit for two minutes without solving anything. Just come—as you are.
heavyHope7.prayer: Jesus, I am heavy laden. I come for rest. Teach me Your meekness. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: God of all comfort
heavyHope7.text: Blessed be God, even the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all comfort; Who comforteth us in all our tribulation, that we may be able to comfort them which are in any trouble, by the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.
heavyHope7.speaker: Paul — writing from his own affliction
heavyHope7.plain: Comfort here starts with who God is—not with you having it together. He comforts in tribulation; later that same comfort might bless someone else.
heavyHope7.today: Thank Him for one small comfort you have received—even if it felt fragile.
heavyHope7.action: Send a two-line encouragement to one person, or pray quietly for someone who feels like you do.
heavyHope7.prayer: Father of mercies, comfort me in my tribulation. Use it someday to comfort another. Amen.

heavyHope7.title: Trade anxiety for peace
heavyHope7.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
heavyHope7.speaker: Paul — from prison, not from ease
heavyHope7.plain: Seven days does not erase depression. It gives you a rhythm: request, thanks, peace that guards heart and mind when understanding cannot explain it.
heavyHope7.today: Finish this week by naming three requests and three thanks—out loud if you can.
heavyHope7.action: Bookmark this plan or add a calendar note to reopen it when the fog returns.
heavyHope7.prayer: Lord, thank You for these seven days. Let Your peace guard my heart and mind in Christ Jesus. Amen.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: You Are Not Forgotten
singlenessLoneliness7.text: I say therefore to the unmarried and widows, It is good for them if they abide even as I.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: Paul — who served single, honoring both gift and calling
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: Paul, who was single, says it can be good to stay as you are right now. God is not disappointed in your situation — He can use this season for something beautiful.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: Many mornings I woke up to quiet rooms and wondered if God noticed the ache. He did. He still does.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: Write down one thing you can do today that honors the Lord with undivided attention (big or small).
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Lord, help me see this day as a gift, not a punishment. I give You my loneliness.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: God Sets the Lonely in Families
singlenessLoneliness7.text: God setteth the solitary in families: he bringeth out those which are bound with chains: but the rebellious dwell in a dry land.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: The psalmist — ascribing praise in the congregation
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: God places lonely people into families — sometimes blood, sometimes church, sometimes new friendships. He brings freedom.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: The family you long for might look different than you pictured. That's okay. He's building something real.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: Reach out to one person (text, call, or pray for them) as if they're part of your God-given family today.
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Father, set me in the family You have for me. Open my eyes to the people around me.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: He Will Never Leave You
singlenessLoneliness7.text: And the LORD, he it is that doth go before thee; he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee: fear not, neither be dismayed.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: Moses — to Israel and Joshua before the next hard step
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: Even if people leave or relationships change, the Lord goes ahead of you and stays with you. Always.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: Divorce or long singleness can make trust feel risky. God is the safest place to put your heart.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: Speak Deuteronomy 31:8 out loud once today when the quiet feels heavy.
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Lord, I feel alone sometimes, but I choose to believe You are with me right now.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: Your Maker Is Your Husband
singlenessLoneliness7.text: For thy Maker is thine husband; the LORD of hosts is his name; and thy Redeemer the Holy One of Israel, The God of the whole earth shall he be called.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: Isaiah — to Zion, of covenant love that outlasts every earthly story
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: God calls Himself your Maker and Husband. He is committed to you with a love deeper than any marriage.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: This verse has carried many through divorce or long waiting. You are not "less than" — you are deeply loved.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: Take 5 quiet minutes and thank God for one way He has provided for you this week.
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Jesus, be my closest companion today. Remind me I belong to You.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: When Family Feels Far
singlenessLoneliness7.text: When my father and my mother forsake me, then the LORD will take me up.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: David — after foes, before "seek ye my face"
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: Even if parents, spouse, or friends have let you down, the Lord will pick you up and care for you.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: Rejection stings deeply after divorce or in singleness. God steps in where others stepped away.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: Do one small act of kindness for yourself today — the same grace you'd show a friend.
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Lord, heal the places that still hurt. Hold me when others can't.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: I Am With You Always
singlenessLoneliness7.text: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: Jesus — sending His disciples; His last promise on the mountain
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: Jesus' last promise: I am with you always — through every season, every night, every lonely moment.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: The ache may not vanish overnight, but His presence is steady. You are never truly by yourself.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: End the day by writing one thing you noticed about God's nearness today (even tiny).
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Thank You for never leaving. Help me feel Your presence tonight.

singlenessLoneliness7.title: Cast Your Care on Him
singlenessLoneliness7.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
singlenessLoneliness7.speaker: Peter — to exiles who knew pressure and quiet rooms
singlenessLoneliness7.plain: Hand over the worries, the what-ifs, the longing. He genuinely cares about every part of your heart.
singlenessLoneliness7.today: You've carried enough alone. Today is a good day to hand more of it over.
singlenessLoneliness7.action: Choose one worry or longing and intentionally "cast" it by writing it down and setting the paper aside (or deleting the note).
singlenessLoneliness7.prayer: Lord, I give You my future, my desires, and my pain. I trust You care for me.

kidsAnxiety7.title: Fear Not — God Is With Us
kidsAnxiety7.text: Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: God through Isaiah — to scared hearts, young and grown
kidsAnxiety7.plain: God speaks directly to fearful hearts — including our children's and ours. He promises strength and help even when we feel weak.
kidsAnxiety7.today: Many nights I've held a scared child and felt just as scared myself. God is holding both of us.
kidsAnxiety7.action: Sit with your child today and read Isaiah 41:10 together slowly. Let them hold the Bible if they want.
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Lord, calm my child's heart and mine. Remind us You are near.

kidsAnxiety7.title: Cast All Our Cares
kidsAnxiety7.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: Peter — to believers under real pressure
kidsAnxiety7.plain: We can hand over every worry — the big ones and the little bedtime ones. God genuinely cares.
kidsAnxiety7.today: Kids often carry worries they don't know how to name. Naming them together and giving them to God is powerful.
kidsAnxiety7.action: Make a simple "worry box" or note with your child. Write one fear and pray over it together.
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Father, we cast our cares on You because You care for us and for my child.

kidsAnxiety7.title: Peace That Guards the Heart
kidsAnxiety7.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: Paul — from prison, not from ease
kidsAnxiety7.plain: Instead of worrying, we can pray and thank God. His peace can guard our children's hearts and minds.
kidsAnxiety7.today: Teaching kids to pray instead of panic is one of the best gifts we can give them.
kidsAnxiety7.action: When anxiety shows up today, pause and pray Philippians 4:6-7 out loud with your child.
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Lord, give my child Your peace that passes understanding.

kidsAnxiety7.title: Train Up a Child
kidsAnxiety7.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: Solomon — wisdom for parents who plant seeds daily
kidsAnxiety7.plain: We are planting seeds of trust in God. Even small, consistent moments matter.
kidsAnxiety7.today: You don't have to have all the answers. Just point them to the One who does.
kidsAnxiety7.action: Share one short story of a time God helped you or your family in the past.
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Help me train my child in Your ways with patience and love.

kidsAnxiety7.title: You Are More Valuable
kidsAnxiety7.text: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: Jesus — teaching the Twelve how the Father watches
kidsAnxiety7.plain: God cares about every detail of our children's lives. They are deeply valuable to Him.
kidsAnxiety7.today: Kids need to hear they matter — not because they perform, but because they are His.
kidsAnxiety7.action: Tell your child one specific way you see God's care for them (or for your family).
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Thank You that my child is precious to You. Number their days with peace.

kidsAnxiety7.title: Be Still and Know
kidsAnxiety7.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: The sons of Korah — a stillness command in the storm Psalm
kidsAnxiety7.plain: In the middle of big feelings, we can stop, breathe, and remember God is in control.
kidsAnxiety7.today: Sometimes the most powerful thing we do as parents is simply be still together with God.
kidsAnxiety7.action: Practice 60 seconds of quiet breathing and saying "God is with us" with your child.
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Lord, help us be still and know You are God.

kidsAnxiety7.title: Trust in the Lord
kidsAnxiety7.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
kidsAnxiety7.speaker: Solomon — father to son, on the core of wisdom
kidsAnxiety7.plain: We don't have to understand everything. We just trust and acknowledge Him — for ourselves and our kids.
kidsAnxiety7.today: Parenting through anxiety reminds us how much we also need to trust God daily.
kidsAnxiety7.action: End the week by thanking God for one small step of peace you've seen this week (in your child or yourself).
kidsAnxiety7.prayer: Lord, we trust You with our family. Direct our paths.

sleepRest7.title: The Lord Gives Sleep
sleepRest7.text: It is vain for you to rise up early, to sit up late, to eat the bread of sorrows: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.
sleepRest7.speaker: Solomon — a song of degrees for builders who cannot outwork God
sleepRest7.plain: God is not impressed by our all-night worrying. He lovingly gives real sleep to His children.
sleepRest7.today: Many nights I stared at the ceiling replaying the day. God gently reminded me He was still in control.
sleepRest7.action: Before bed tonight, say out loud: 'The Lord gives sleep to His beloved.'
sleepRest7.prayer: Father, I am Your beloved. Please give me the gift of rest tonight.

sleepRest7.title: I Will Both Lay Me Down in Peace
sleepRest7.text: I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.
sleepRest7.speaker: David — when trouble pressed, before morning
sleepRest7.plain: David chose to lie down in peace even when surrounded by trouble. The Lord keeps us safe.
sleepRest7.today: Safety is not the absence of problems — it is the presence of God while we sleep.
sleepRest7.action: Place your hand on your chest and slowly pray Psalm 4:8 before turning out the light.
sleepRest7.prayer: Lord, I lay down in peace because You make me dwell in safety.

sleepRest7.title: When My Heart Is Overwhelmed
sleepRest7.text: From the end of the earth will I cry unto thee, when my heart is overwhelmed: lead me to the rock that is higher than I.
sleepRest7.speaker: David — far from home, heart full
sleepRest7.plain: When thoughts race and sleep feels impossible, we can cry out. God leads us to a higher place.
sleepRest7.today: Nighttime can make every fear feel bigger. God is still bigger.
sleepRest7.action: Write down the loudest worry on a piece of paper and set it aside until morning.
sleepRest7.prayer: Lord, my heart feels overwhelmed. Lead me to You, my Rock.

sleepRest7.title: He Gives His Beloved Sleep
sleepRest7.text: for so he giveth his beloved sleep.
sleepRest7.speaker: Solomon — the closing line of a verse about grace, not grinding
sleepRest7.plain: You don't have to earn rest. Because you are loved by Him, He wants you to sleep.
sleepRest7.today: Grace applies even to bedtime. You are not failing if sleep takes time.
sleepRest7.action: Thank God for three things from the day (even small ones) before closing your eyes.
sleepRest7.prayer: Thank You that I am Your beloved. Help me receive Your gift of sleep.

sleepRest7.title: The Peace of God Shall Keep You
sleepRest7.text: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
sleepRest7.speaker: Paul — from prison, after prayer and thanksgiving
sleepRest7.plain: God's peace can guard your heart and mind while you sleep — even when you don't understand everything.
sleepRest7.today: Racing thoughts lose power when we hand them to the One who never sleeps.
sleepRest7.action: Play or read Philippians 4:6-7 quietly if you wake up in the night.
sleepRest7.prayer: Let Your peace guard my heart and mind tonight, Jesus.

sleepRest7.title: He That Keepeth Israel
sleepRest7.text: Behold, he that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep.
sleepRest7.speaker: A pilgrim's song — the LORD as night watchman
sleepRest7.plain: While you sleep, God never does. He is watching over you all night long.
sleepRest7.today: You can rest because the One who loves you is wide awake.
sleepRest7.action: Picture God standing guard over your home and family as you fall asleep.
sleepRest7.prayer: Thank You for watching over me while I sleep. I am safe in You.

sleepRest7.title: Return to Your Rest
sleepRest7.text: Return unto thy rest, O my soul; for the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee.
sleepRest7.speaker: The psalmist — after trouble, before the cup of salvation
sleepRest7.plain: Even after hard days or anxious nights, we can speak to our own soul and return to rest.
sleepRest7.today: God has been good to you this week. Your soul can settle because of His kindness.
sleepRest7.action: End this plan by writing one way God has been good to you this week.
sleepRest7.prayer: Lord, I return to rest. You have dealt bountifully with me.

psalmsComfort7.title: The Lord is my shepherd
psalmsComfort7.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
psalmsComfort7.speaker: David — the shepherd-king, before the dark valley
psalmsComfort7.plain: Comfort begins with belonging. You are not self-led in the noise—you have a Shepherd who does not lose sheep.
psalmsComfort7.today: What are you trying to supply for yourself that He already names as His job?
psalmsComfort7.action: Whisper the first line of this psalm once before you touch your phone today.
psalmsComfort7.prayer: Lord, be my Shepherd. Teach my soul to stop grasping and start following. Amen.

psalmsComfort7.title: Near the broken heart
psalmsComfort7.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
psalmsComfort7.speaker: David — after fear, after deliverance
psalmsComfort7.plain: God does not wait for you to glue your heart back together. He draws near while it is still cracked.
psalmsComfort7.today: Where does it feel like your spirit is crushed—and can you tell Him without fixing your tone first?
psalmsComfort7.action: Write one honest sentence of grief or anxiety and end it with: "You are nigh."
psalmsComfort7.prayer: Lord, my heart is broken. Draw near. Save me in the contrite place. Amen.

psalmsComfort7.title: Refuge when trouble is loud
psalmsComfort7.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
psalmsComfort7.speaker: The sons of Korah — a song for shaky ground
psalmsComfort7.plain: Trouble is not proof He left. He is not a distant refuge—He is present help while the ground still moves.
psalmsComfort7.today: What trouble is trying to name itself as "God is gone"?
psalmsComfort7.action: Name the trouble out loud, then say: "Very present help." Pause five seconds.
psalmsComfort7.prayer: God, be my refuge and strength today—not someday. Right now. Amen.

psalmsComfort7.title: Light when fear names the room
psalmsComfort7.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
psalmsComfort7.speaker: David — when enemies were real, not imagined
psalmsComfort7.plain: Fear shrinks when you remember who lights the path and who holds your life—not your nerves.
psalmsComfort7.today: Which fear is loudest—and what truth from this verse answers it without shouting?
psalmsComfort7.action: Replace one "what if" today with: "The Lord is my light and my salvation."
psalmsComfort7.prayer: Lord, be my light. Let fear step back when You step in. Amen.

psalmsComfort7.title: Rest under His shadow
psalmsComfort7.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
psalmsComfort7.speaker: A song of shelter — for the one who stays close
psalmsComfort7.plain: Comfort is not always a feeling. Sometimes it is shadow—cover you did not earn, shade because you stayed near.
psalmsComfort7.today: Where are you living exposed—trying to be your own cover?
psalmsComfort7.action: Sit for two minutes without solving anything. Abide: stay in one place with Him.
psalmsComfort7.prayer: Most High, let me dwell in Your secret place. I want Your shadow, not my strain. Amen.

psalmsComfort7.title: Where help comes from
psalmsComfort7.text: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
psalmsComfort7.speaker: A pilgrim song — for the journey you did not choose
psalmsComfort7.plain: Help is not invented inside your chest. It comes from the Lord who keeps your going out and your coming in.
psalmsComfort7.today: What hill are you staring at—diagnosis, silence, money, pain—and can you lift your eyes past it to Him?
psalmsComfort7.action: Look out a window or at the sky once and pray one sentence: "My help comes from You."
psalmsComfort7.prayer: Lord, I lift my eyes. My help comes from You—not from the size of the hill. Amen.

psalmsComfort7.title: Known all the way through
psalmsComfort7.text: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.
psalmsComfort7.speaker: David — before the wonder of being formed and seen
psalmsComfort7.plain: You are not a problem to figure out alone. The God who searches you is not gathering evidence against you—He already knows, and He stays.
psalmsComfort7.today: What part of you feels hidden, ashamed, or too much—and what changes if He knows it and still draws near?
psalmsComfort7.action: Finish this line on paper: "Because You know me, I can tell You __________."
psalmsComfort7.prayer: Lord, You have searched me and known me. Thank You for love that knows all of me. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Where wisdom starts
proverbsWisdom7.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — father to son — first lesson
proverbsWisdom7.plain: Wisdom does not begin with self-confidence. It begins with awe that fits God—not fear that runs from Him.
proverbsWisdom7.today: Where are you still trying to be your own smartest voice?
proverbsWisdom7.action: Before one decision today, pause and say: "What if fearing the Lord mattered more than looking smart?"
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Lord, be the beginning of my knowledge. Teach me not to despise instruction. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Lean off your own map
proverbsWisdom7.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — same father, same steady hand
proverbsWisdom7.plain: Your understanding can be sincere and still wrong. Trust is whole-heart weight—not half on God, half on your read of the room.
proverbsWisdom7.today: What are you leaning on—schedule, anger, control—that is really "thine own understanding"?
proverbsWisdom7.action: Write one situation where you will trust first, plan second.
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Lord, I trust You with all my heart. I lean off my own understanding. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Knowledge of the holy
proverbsWisdom7.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — wisdom personified calls
proverbsWisdom7.plain: Wisdom is not a vibe. It starts with knowing who God is—holy—and letting that reorder you.
proverbsWisdom7.today: Where do you need "understanding" that lines up with God's character, not just what feels workable?
proverbsWisdom7.action: Read this verse twice slowly. Underline one word in your mind to carry today.
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Holy God, be the beginning of my wisdom. Give me understanding that honors You. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Soft answer
proverbsWisdom7.text: A soft answer turneth away wrath: but grievous words stir up anger.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — watching words land
proverbsWisdom7.plain: You cannot control someone else's heat. You can choose a soft answer so wrath does not get more fuel.
proverbsWisdom7.today: Where is a hard word waiting on your tongue?
proverbsWisdom7.action: Send or speak one sentence that is softer than your first draft—without being fake.
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Lord, let my answer be soft enough to turn wrath away. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Commit the works
proverbsWisdom7.text: Commit thy works unto the LORD, and thy thoughts shall be established.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — on work and clarity
proverbsWisdom7.plain: Clarity often follows surrender. Commit the works—not just the worry about them.
proverbsWisdom7.today: What project, conversation, or burden have you not actually handed to Him?
proverbsWisdom7.action: Name one "work" out loud: "I commit this to You." Then do the next small faithful step.
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Lord, I commit my works to You. Establish my thoughts. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Train and tend
proverbsWisdom7.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — long view on formation
proverbsWisdom7.plain: Training is direction over drama. It is faithful repetition—not perfect performance.
proverbsWisdom7.today: Who are you shaping—a child, a student, your own habits—and what "way" are you actually showing?
proverbsWisdom7.action: One concrete act of patience or instruction today that matches the way you say you want to go.
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Lord, help me train faithfully. Give me patience for the long arc. Amen.

proverbsWisdom7.title: Praise that lasts
proverbsWisdom7.text: Favour is deceitful, and beauty is vain: but a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised.
proverbsWisdom7.speaker: Solomon — closing a poem of strength
proverbsWisdom7.plain: What flatters fades. What fears the Lord and walks in truth lasts—and gets named with honor.
proverbsWisdom7.today: Where are you chasing favor or image instead of fearing the Lord?
proverbsWisdom7.action: Thank God for one person whose faithfulness is deeper than appearance.
proverbsWisdom7.prayer: Lord, let fearing You be what I want praised in me. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: The God of hope
hopeUncertainty7.text: Now the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that ye may abound in hope, through the power of the Holy Ghost.
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: Paul — blessing believers with hope that overflows
hopeUncertainty7.plain: Hope here is not a mood. It is supplied—filled—by the God who is hope Himself.
hopeUncertainty7.today: Where does your hope feel thin—and can you ask to abound, not just survive?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Pray one sentence: "Fill me with joy and peace in believing." Mean it slowly.
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: God of hope, fill me. Let me abound in hope by Your Spirit. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: Anchor inside the veil
hopeUncertainty7.text: Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast, and which entereth into that within the veil;
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: The writer of Hebrews — hope that holds in storms
hopeUncertainty7.plain: When the future is fog, hope is not a guess. It is anchored—sure—inside the veil where Christ has gone before you.
hopeUncertainty7.today: What anxiety feels like drifting—and what would it change to picture an anchor set?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Draw a small anchor on paper or in notes; write one word beside it: "stedfast."
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: Lord, my soul needs an anchor. Hold me sure inside the veil. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: Wait in His word
hopeUncertainty7.text: I wait for the LORD, my soul doth wait, and in his word do I hope.
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: The psalmist — out of the depths, still waiting
hopeUncertainty7.plain: Waiting is not doing nothing. It is aiming your hope at His word—not at the news feed.
hopeUncertainty7.today: What are you waiting for—and have you brought that wait to Scripture?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Read Psalm 130:5 five times. Let your soul wait one minute in silence.
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: Lord, I wait for You. In Your word I hope. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: Rejoice, endure, pray
hopeUncertainty7.text: Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer;
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: Paul — practical theology for hard weeks
hopeUncertainty7.plain: Hope does not cancel tribulation. It gives you patience inside it—and prayer keeps the line open.
hopeUncertainty7.today: Which of the three—rejoicing, patience, prayer—needs your attention most today?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Do a sixty-second prayer walk: one thank-you, one honest tribulation line, one request.
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: Lord, I rejoice in hope. Make me patient. Keep me instant in prayer. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: Strength for the wait
hopeUncertainty7.text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: Isaiah — to exiles who felt finished
hopeUncertainty7.plain: Waiting on the Lord is not stalled living. It is how strength gets renewed when you have none left.
hopeUncertainty7.today: Are you trying to sprint answers—or wait long enough for strength to return?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Sit still three minutes. No phone. Whisper: "I wait upon the LORD."
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: Lord, renew my strength. I wait on You. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: Expectation from Him
hopeUncertainty7.text: My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from him.
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: David — when power and betrayal pressed in
hopeUncertainty7.plain: Expectation is pointed somewhere. Aim it at Him only—so disappointment does not own your week.
hopeUncertainty7.today: What expectation have you pinned on a person or outcome that belongs first on God?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Rewrite one hope as a sentence starting with: "My expectation is from God for..."
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: Lord, my soul waits only on You. My expectation is from You. Amen.

hopeUncertainty7.title: Hope and quiet waiting
hopeUncertainty7.text: The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him. The LORD is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the LORD.
hopeUncertainty7.speaker: Jeremiah — after honest grief, choosing hope
hopeUncertainty7.plain: Hope here is stubborn loyalty to God's goodness—not denial of pain. Quiet waiting is strength, not weakness.
hopeUncertainty7.today: What would "quiet waiting" look like in your loudest worry?
hopeUncertainty7.action: Finish seven days by writing: "Because of hope in Him, I will quietly wait for __________."
hopeUncertainty7.prayer: Lord, You are my portion. I hope in You. Teach me quiet waiting. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: In the beginning
gospelJohn7.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
gospelJohn7.speaker: John — opening his Gospel
gospelJohn7.plain: Before your week started, the Word was. Your story does not begin with chaos—it begins with Christ.
gospelJohn7.today: What feels like "beginning" in your life right now—and who is really first?
gospelJohn7.action: Read John 1:1–5 in the chapter reader when you can. Let the first verse settle.
gospelJohn7.prayer: Lord, You are the Word. Be first in my mind today. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: God so loved
gospelJohn7.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
gospelJohn7.speaker: Jesus — speaking to Nicodemus by night
gospelJohn7.plain: Love moved first. Believing is not earning—it is receiving what was already given.
gospelJohn7.today: Where do you feel "perishing" in worry or habit—and can you believe He gave His Son for that too?
gospelJohn7.action: Say John 3:16 out loud once. Let "whosoever" include you.
gospelJohn7.prayer: Father, thank You for giving Your Son. I believe; hold me in everlasting life. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: Living water
gospelJohn7.text: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
gospelJohn7.speaker: Jesus — at the well with a woman who knew thirst
gospelJohn7.plain: Thirst returns when you drink from the wrong wells. He offers water that becomes a spring inside you.
gospelJohn7.today: What are you drinking from—approval, escape, control—that leaves you thirsty again?
gospelJohn7.action: Drink a glass of water slowly. Pray: "Lord, be my living water today."
gospelJohn7.prayer: Jesus, spring up in me. I want water that lasts. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: Bread of life
gospelJohn7.text: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
gospelJohn7.speaker: Jesus — after the feeding of the five thousand
gospelJohn7.plain: Hungry souls need more than distraction. Coming to Him is how hunger and thirst get answered.
gospelJohn7.today: What are you "feeding" on that is not bread?
gospelJohn7.action: Come to Him in one honest sentence before your next meal.
gospelJohn7.prayer: Lord, I come. Be my bread of life. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: The good shepherd
gospelJohn7.text: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
gospelJohn7.speaker: Jesus — naming His care and His cost
gospelJohn7.plain: A good shepherd does not abandon sheep when wolves come. He gives His life—so you are not left alone.
gospelJohn7.today: Where do you feel like scattered sheep—and can you listen for His voice?
gospelJohn7.action: Name one way you will follow one small step of obedience today.
gospelJohn7.prayer: Good Shepherd, I hear You. Lead me. Thank You for laying down Your life. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: The way, truth, life
gospelJohn7.text: Jesus saith unto him, I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
gospelJohn7.speaker: Jesus — comforting troubled disciples
gospelJohn7.plain: When the path is unclear, He does not only point a way—He is the way. Truth and life come with Him.
gospelJohn7.today: What feels blocked—and can you bring it to the Way, not just to worry?
gospelJohn7.action: Write "way, truth, life" on a card. Glance at it when anxiety narrows your view.
gospelJohn7.prayer: Lord, You are my way, truth, and life. Bring me to the Father. Amen.

gospelJohn7.title: Written that ye might believe
gospelJohn7.text: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
gospelJohn7.speaker: John — stating why he wrote
gospelJohn7.plain: This Gospel is for faith that turns into life—not information that stays on the page.
gospelJohn7.today: After seven days in John, what do you believe more clearly about Jesus—and what life does that ask of you?
gospelJohn7.action: Tell God one sentence of thanks for something you saw in John this week.
gospelJohn7.prayer: Lord, I believe Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God. Give me life through His name. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Delivered for His will
galatiansFreedom7.text: Who gave himself for our sins, that he might deliver us from this present evil world, according to the will of God and our Father:
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — opening shot: grace before rules
galatiansFreedom7.plain: Christ gave Himself—first—to deliver you from a world system that trains you to perform. The will of God starts with rescue, not scorekeeping.
galatiansFreedom7.today: Where do you still feel measured instead of loved?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Say slowly: "He gave Himself for my sins—to deliver me." Let it land.
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Lord, deliver me from performance religion. I receive Your will. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Crucified with Christ
galatiansFreedom7.text: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — the center of Christian identity
galatiansFreedom7.plain: Your old self-justifying life ended at the cross. What lives now is Christ in you—by faith, not flexing.
galatiansFreedom7.today: Where are you still trying to be "I" instead of letting Christ live?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Write one sentence: "Not I—but Christ in me—in __________."
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Jesus, I am crucified with You. Live in me where I keep grabbing the wheel. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Redeemed from the curse
galatiansFreedom7.text: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree:
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — explaining the cross in plain terms
galatiansFreedom7.plain: The curse the law pronounces—Christ carried it. You are not buying your way back; you are redeemed.
galatiansFreedom7.today: What guilt still sounds like a curse—and needs the tree?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Read the verse once, then thank God for one specific mercy you could not earn.
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Lord, You were made a curse for me. Thank You. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Abba, Father
galatiansFreedom7.text: And because ye are sons, God hath sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying, Abba, Father.
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — adoption, not orphan fear
galatiansFreedom7.plain: The Spirit does not coach you from the sidelines—He cries from inside you toward a Father who receives you.
galatiansFreedom7.today: When did you last pray "Abba" like a child—not like a defendant?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Pray one sentence starting with "Abba" about what you need today.
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Abba, Father, I am Yours. Receive me again. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Stand fast in liberty
galatiansFreedom7.text: Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — liberty as a posture, not chaos
galatiansFreedom7.plain: Freedom is not "do whatever." It is standing—unshaken—in what Christ won. Watch what tries to yoke you again.
galatiansFreedom7.today: What old yoke is knocking—approval, addiction to control, fear of man?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Name one yoke. Say: "I stand fast in liberty." Mean it once.
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Lord, I stand fast in liberty. Do not let me go back to bondage. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Walk in the Spirit
galatiansFreedom7.text: If we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit.
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — after the fruit of the Spirit
galatiansFreedom7.plain: Life in the Spirit is not a mood; it is a walk—daily, step by step—when feelings rise and fall.
galatiansFreedom7.today: Where does your walk look like the flesh winning today—and what would one Spirit step look like?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Before your next hard conversation, whisper: "Walk in the Spirit."
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Spirit of God, I live in You—teach my feet to walk with You today. Amen.

galatiansFreedom7.title: Do not lose heart
galatiansFreedom7.text: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
galatiansFreedom7.speaker: Paul — closing a letter about freedom and love
galatiansFreedom7.plain: Freedom produces fruit that takes time. Weariness is not failure—fainting is quitting what love started.
galatiansFreedom7.today: What "well doing" feels unrewarded—and needs patience, not proof?
galatiansFreedom7.action: Finish seven days by writing one line of encouragement to yourself from this letter.
galatiansFreedom7.prayer: Lord, I am weary but I faint not in You. In due season, let me reap. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: Glory in tribulation
sufferingEndure7.text: And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also: knowing that tribulation worketh patience; And patience, experience; and experience, hope:
sufferingEndure7.speaker: Paul — chains clanking, hope still standing
sufferingEndure7.plain: Paul is not pretending pain is fun. He names a chain: pressure shapes patience, patience proves real, and proof deepens hope. None of that erases the tribulation—it gives it somewhere to go.
sufferingEndure7.today: Where is tribulation pressing you—and can you tell God the truth about it without faking cheer?
sufferingEndure7.action: Write one hard thing, then write one word after it: patience, experience, or hope—whichever fits today.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: Lord, I do not pretend this is easy. Work patience in me. Let hope grow. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: Let patience finish
sufferingEndure7.text: My brethren, count it all joy when ye fall into divers temptations; Knowing this, that the trying of your faith worketh patience. But let patience have her perfect work, that ye may be perfect and entire, wanting nothing.
sufferingEndure7.speaker: James — to people who knew pressure
sufferingEndure7.plain: Joy here is not a fake smile. It is knowing trials are not wasted—faith is being exercised. Let patience finish; God is not in a hurry to leave you half-formed.
sufferingEndure7.today: What temptation or trial is testing you—and what would "patience having her perfect work" look like today?
sufferingEndure7.action: When stress spikes once today, pause ten seconds before you speak. Let patience get one word in first.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: Lord, let patience have her perfect work. Make me entire, not just reactive. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: Weak, then strong
sufferingEndure7.text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my infirmities, that the power of Christ may rest upon me. Therefore I take pleasure in infirmities, in reproaches, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ's sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.
sufferingEndure7.speaker: Paul — the thorn still present, grace louder
sufferingEndure7.plain: Christ's power rests where you cannot muscle through. Weakness is not failure—it is room for Him.
sufferingEndure7.today: Where do you feel weakest—and can you stop apologizing to God for needing grace there?
sufferingEndure7.action: Say aloud: "Your strength is made perfect in weakness." Mean it once.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: Lord, Your grace is sufficient. Let Your power rest on my weakness. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: After ye have suffered a while
sufferingEndure7.text: But the God of all grace, who hath called us unto his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after that ye have suffered a while, make you perfect, stablish, strengthen, settle you.
sufferingEndure7.speaker: Peter — to exiles who knew ache
sufferingEndure7.plain: "A while" can feel endless. God does not mock that. He promises to use suffering as a passage—not the final word—and to set you firm on the other side.
sufferingEndure7.today: What part of your life still feels unsettled—and can you trust the God of all grace with the timeline?
sufferingEndure7.action: Circle one area where you need to be "stablished." Pray that word once, slowly.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: God of all grace, after suffering, establish and strengthen me. Settle me in You. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: Looking unto Jesus
sufferingEndure7.text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
sufferingEndure7.speaker: The writer of Hebrews — to runners getting tired
sufferingEndure7.plain: You are not sprinting for applause. You run with patience because Jesus already ran through shame and finished. Eyes on Him—not on the hecklers.
sufferingEndure7.today: What weight or besetting sin is slowing your run—and what would laying it aside look like today?
sufferingEndure7.action: Read verse 2 once more. Whisper "Looking unto Jesus" before your next hard task.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: Lord, I lay aside what I can. I look to Jesus, author and finisher. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: Patience with joyfulness
sufferingEndure7.text: Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;
sufferingEndure7.speaker: Paul — praying for a church under pressure
sufferingEndure7.plain: Patience does not have to be grim. His might can hold you in longsuffering and still leave room for joy—not denial, but deep breath.
sufferingEndure7.today: Where is longsuffering draining you—and could you ask for one small joy today that does not insult your pain?
sufferingEndure7.action: Thank God for one small mercy out loud—food, breath, a friend, sleep.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: Strengthen me with all might, Lord—unto patience and longsuffering with joyfulness. Amen.

sufferingEndure7.title: The glory ahead
sufferingEndure7.text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
sufferingEndure7.speaker: Paul — who knew suffering by experience
sufferingEndure7.plain: This does not erase today. It measures it against a weight of glory you have not seen yet. Christ in you is the first taste; the full reveal is coming.
