sufferingEndure7.today: After seven days, what suffering feels heaviest—and can you hand it to the God who calls glory "not worthy to be compared"?
sufferingEndure7.action: Write one line of hope that is honest—not hype—for the week ahead.
sufferingEndure7.prayer: Lord, the sufferings are real. So is the glory. Hold me till it is revealed. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: Enter with thanksgiving
psalmsPraise7.text: Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all ye lands. Serve the LORD with gladness: come before his presence with singing. Know ye that the LORD he is God: it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture. Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name. For the LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations.
psalmsPraise7.speaker: The psalmist — a door flung open
psalmsPraise7.plain: Praise is not performance. It is coming in noisy or quiet, knowing you belong—sheep with a good Shepherd, not orphans faking strength.
psalmsPraise7.today: What would "serve the LORD with gladness" look like in your actual Tuesday?
psalmsPraise7.action: Sing or hum one line of this psalm in the car, shower, or kitchen.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: Lord, I enter with thanksgiving. You are good; Your mercy outlasts my mood. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: Forget not His benefits
psalmsPraise7.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases; Who redeemeth thy life from destruction; who crowneth thee with lovingkindness and tender mercies; Who satisfieth thy mouth with good things; so that thy youth is renewed like the eagle's.
psalmsPraise7.speaker: David — talking to his own soul
psalmsPraise7.plain: Your soul needs directing, not just comfort. Blessing starts with remembering—forgiveness, healing, rescue—before you demand the next thing.
psalmsPraise7.today: Which benefit do you forget first—forgiveness, healing, rescue—and can you name it back to God?
psalmsPraise7.action: List three benefits on paper or in notes. Read them aloud.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: Bless the LORD, O my soul—and all within me. I forget not Your benefits. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: Sing to the Rock
psalmsPraise7.text: O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms. For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods. In his hand are the deep places of the earth: the strength of the hills is his also. The sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. O come, let us worship and bow down: let us kneel before the LORD our maker. For he is our God; and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. To day if ye will hear his voice,
psalmsPraise7.speaker: The psalmist — from song to kneeling
psalmsPraise7.plain: Praise moves your body—voice, knees—because God is not a small thought. He holds depths and heights; you are sheep, not owners of the pasture.
psalmsPraise7.today: Where has your heart been too proud to kneel—and can you kneel in spirit if not in body?
psalmsPraise7.action: Stand or kneel for one minute. Offer one sentence of praise before you move on.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: Rock of my salvation, I worship You—great King, my Maker. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: Let everything praise
psalmsPraise7.text: Praise ye the LORD. Praise God in his sanctuary: praise him in the firmament of his power. Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his excellent greatness. Praise him with the sound of the trumpet: praise him with psaltery and harp. Praise him with timbrel and dance: praise him with stringed instruments and organs. Praise him upon the loud cymbals: praise him upon the high sounding cymbals. Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.
psalmsPraise7.speaker: The psalms — ending the book with noise and breath
psalmsPraise7.plain: Instruments and breath—God welcomes loud praise. If you have breath, you have a reason. Start there.
psalmsPraise7.today: What "instrument" do you have today—voice, hands, work, care for kids—and can you aim it toward praise once?
psalmsPraise7.action: Clap once, tap a rhythm, or speak "Praise ye the LORD" before bed.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: Let my breath praise You, LORD. Praise ye the LORD. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: Morning and night
psalmsPraise7.text: It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High: To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning, and thy faithfulness every night, Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the psaltery; upon the harp with a solemn sound. For thou, LORD, hast made me glad through thy work: I will triumph in the works of thy hands.
psalmsPraise7.speaker: The psalmist — a rhythm of thanks
psalmsPraise7.plain: Morning and night bracket the day. Praise does not require a perfect day—only honest noticing of His lovingkindness and faithfulness.
psalmsPraise7.today: What can you thank Him for this morning, and what from today will you thank Him for tonight?
psalmsPraise7.action: Set two phone reminders: one word of thanks at each.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: Most High, I show forth Your lovingkindness in the morning and Your faithfulness at night. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: Great is the Lord
psalmsPraise7.text: I will extol thee, my God, O king; and I will bless thy name for ever and ever. Every day will I bless thee; and I will praise thy name for ever and ever. Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised; and his greatness is unsearchable.
psalmsPraise7.speaker: David — extolling with no expiration date
psalmsPraise7.plain: Praise is daily, not a spike. His greatness has no bottom—you will not run out of reasons.
psalmsPraise7.today: What one attribute of God—kindness, strength, nearness—can you extol today without rushing?
psalmsPraise7.action: Bless His name once an hour for three waking hours—one short sentence each time.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: Great is the LORD. I bless Your name today—and the next day. Amen.

psalmsPraise7.title: His wonderful works
psalmsPraise7.text: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever. Oh that men would praise the LORD for his goodness, and for his wonderful works to the children of men!
psalmsPraise7.speaker: The psalmist — after stories of rescue, the same refrain
psalmsPraise7.plain: Psalm 107 tells storm, prison, sickness, and trouble—then returns to this line after each story (verses 8, 15, 21, 31). Your life may repeat hard themes; His goodness and wonderful works are still the chorus.
psalmsPraise7.today: Where have you seen rescue, even small—and can you join the refrain?
psalmsPraise7.action: Text or tell one person one "wonderful work" you have seen God do.
psalmsPraise7.prayer: O give thanks unto the LORD, for He is good. Let me praise You for Your goodness and wonderful works. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: The word just hit
cancerComfort7.text: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.
cancerComfort7.speaker: David — afraid and still talking to God
cancerComfort7.plain: That moment the doctor said it… everything went quiet and loud at the same time. Your hands shook. Your mind started running every worst-case scenario. You don't have to pretend you're strong right now.
cancerComfort7.today: God doesn't shame you for being afraid. He asks you to bring the fear to Him—even if it's ugly, even if it's screaming.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Right now, say out loud or whisper: “Lord, I'm afraid.” Don't dress it up. Just say it. Second: Write the word cancer on a piece of paper, then write But God… underneath. Leave it somewhere you'll see it today.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Jesus, the word cancer just wrecked me. I'm scared. I don't know what to do with all this fear. I'm trusting You with it anyway. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: I'm so tired already
cancerComfort7.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
cancerComfort7.speaker: Jesus — inviting the worn-out
cancerComfort7.plain: The appointments, the waiting, the scans, the needles—it's only been a few days and you're already exhausted in your soul. You're allowed to be tired.
cancerComfort7.today: Jesus isn't asking you to be brave twenty-four seven. He's inviting the worn-out version of you to come rest on Him.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Find ten quiet minutes today. Sit or lie down and tell Him exactly how tired you are—physically, emotionally, spiritually. Second: Cancel or shorten one non-essential thing today if you can. Give yourself permission to rest without guilt.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Lord, I'm already so tired and this fight just started. Come close. Let me rest in You even when my body won't stop fighting. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: Why me?
cancerComfort7.text: For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
cancerComfort7.speaker: God through Isaiah — His ways are higher
cancerComfort7.plain: The anger and the why me hits hard. You see other people living normal lives while yours feels like it's falling apart. It's okay to feel that.
cancerComfort7.today: God doesn't always explain why, but He promises He's still good and He's still with you in the middle of the why.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Tell God the honest truth today—even if it's “I'm mad at You.” He can take it. Second: Write down three things you're angry about, then write I don't understand, but I'm still Yours at the bottom.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Father, I don't understand why this is happening to me. Some days I'm angry, some days I'm numb. Hold me anyway. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: My body feels like the enemy
cancerComfort7.text: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.
cancerComfort7.speaker: The psalmist — before God who formed him
cancerComfort7.plain: Your own body turned on you. Scans, chemo, radiation—it feels like betrayal from the inside. You look in the mirror and barely recognize yourself.
cancerComfort7.today: Even now, God still calls your body fearfully and wonderfully made. He sees the cancer and He sees you.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Put your hand on the part of your body that hurts most right now and say “Lord, this is Yours too.” Second: Do one small gentle thing for your body today—extra water, soft blanket, favorite pillow—as kindness, not denial.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Jesus, my own body feels like it's fighting me. I feel betrayed. Remind me I'm still Yours—every sick cell, every weak part. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: I feel so alone
cancerComfort7.text: Be strong and of a good courage, fear not, nor be afraid of them: for the LORD thy God, he it is that doth go with thee; he will not fail thee, nor forsake thee.
cancerComfort7.speaker: Moses — charging a frightened people
cancerComfort7.plain: Even when people are around, you can feel completely alone in this fight. The fear is yours. The pain is yours. The unknown is yours.
cancerComfort7.today: God doesn't just send help—He comes with you. He's not watching from a distance.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Talk to Him like He's sitting right beside you in the chemo chair or in the waiting room. Second: Text or call one person today and say “I'm struggling today”—even if it's just one sentence.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Lord, I feel so alone in this. Everyone else gets to live normal days. Don't leave me. Walk with me through every appointment, every night I can't sleep. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: What if I don't make it?
cancerComfort7.text: For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
cancerComfort7.speaker: Paul — writing believers who knew suffering
cancerComfort7.plain: The fear of dying or leaving your family hits different at 3 a.m. You're not weak for thinking about it.
cancerComfort7.today: If the worst happens, it's not the end of your story—just the end of this broken body.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Write a short note to the people you love most—things you want them to know if you don't get to say them later. Second: Read Revelation 21:4 out loud and let yourself cry if you need to.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Father, I'm scared I might not make it. If this is my road, hold my family. And hold me. I want to be with You without pain one day. Amen.

cancerComfort7.title: I'm still here today
cancerComfort7.text: It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
cancerComfort7.speaker: Jeremiah — after honest grief, remembering mercy
cancerComfort7.plain: You made it through another week. Some days you wanted to quit. Some days you just wanted the pain to stop. But you're still here.
cancerComfort7.today: Every new morning is proof God's mercy is still chasing you—even on the worst days of cancer.
cancerComfort7.action: First: Look back at the last seven days and name one small thing you're thankful for—even if it's just I woke up today. Second: Share one honest sentence from this plan on the prayer wall or with someone who loves you.
cancerComfort7.prayer: Lord, thank You I'm still here. Thank You for every hard breath, every tear, every moment You carried me when I couldn't stand. Your mercies really are new. Amen.

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: Gathered in His name
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: Jesus — teaching about life together in His kingdom
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: Family worship does not need a perfect house or a stage. Where two or three gather in His name, He draws near.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: What stands out? Jesus promises His presence when His people gather—not when everything looks polished.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God is not distant while you clear the table or calm a toddler. He meets you in the middle of real rooms.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: Pick one meal or bedtime this week to read this verse aloud together and pause for ten seconds of quiet.
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: Lead without performing: say one sentence about why you need Jesus in the room tonight.
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: Where do you picture Jesus when we are all in the same room?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Pray one short sentence together: "Thank You for being with us."
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Lord, be in the middle of our home—not as a show, but as truth. Thank You for meeting us when we gather in Your name. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw your family together in one room (stick figures are enough). Add a small light or cross where Jesus is "in the midst."
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: When do we feel most "together" at home? When do we feel scattered?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: What words does Jesus use? (two or three, gathered, name, midst.)
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: Why would Jesus care about two or three? What does "in my name" mean for our family?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: How is this different from "good vibes" or a family meeting? What changes if His presence is real?

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: Teach along the way
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: Moses — passing faith to the next generation
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: Faith is meant to ride along with ordinary hours—not only on Sunday.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: Notice when God says to talk: sitting, walking, lying down, rising—normal life.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God ties truth to daily rhythm. He wants His words in the traffic of your day.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: Choose one everyday moment this week (car line, dishes, bedtime) to say one true sentence about God.
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: You will miss moments; grace exists. Name one natural slot this week where you can speak truth without a lecture.
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: What is one place we go every week where we could talk about God for one minute?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Write three words on a sticky note for the fridge: "talk," "walk," "rest"—reminders from this verse.
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Father, help our home sound like Your words—not nagging, not noise, but steady truth in ordinary hours. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw four small pictures: at the table, on a walk, at bedtime, at breakfast—put a heart or Bible symbol in each.
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: What is one busy time when we could still say one thankful sentence to God?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: List the times Moses names. Which one fits our week best?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: What does "diligently" look like for a family—not perfect, but faithful?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: How does this verse challenge phone habits at the table or in the car?

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: Nurture, do not crush
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: Paul — household instructions in Christ
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: Correction can be loving—or it can train a child to flinch. God calls parents toward nurture.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: Two commands: do not provoke; do bring up in the Lord's nurture and instruction.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God cares about the emotional climate of a home—not only outward behavior.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: This week, when correction comes, add one gentle sentence that names love before the rule.
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: Ask yourself: "Am I provoking fear—or nurturing faith?" One honest answer is enough.
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: What helps you feel safe when you mess up—yelling or calm words?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Agree on one family phrase for hard moments, such as: "We fix this together."
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Lord, make our correction nurturing. Train our tone. Let love be louder than frustration. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw a plant being watered (nurture) beside a small spark (provoking). Label them if you want.
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: What is one way we can say hard truth without making someone feel small?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: What is the opposite of provoking, according to Paul?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: What is the difference between anger that clears the air and anger that wounds?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: Where do you see "wrath" build up at home—and what would defuse it?

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: A heritage, not a hassle
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: Solomon — a song of building and belonging
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: On tired days children can feel like tasks. God names them as heritage—a gift with weight and wonder.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: Heritage and reward—language of value, not burden.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God ties children to His generosity, not to our performance as parents.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: Name one child (or one younger friend) with a thankful sentence—out loud—this week.
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: Guilt is loud in parenting. Let gratitude speak once today, even if the day was hard.
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: What is something good God gave you that you did not earn?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Each person finishes: "Thank You for __________ in our family."
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Thank You for the lives You placed in our home. Teach us to treat them as heritage, not hassle. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw a gift tag that says "heritage" on something precious to your family.
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: What is one thing about our family that feels like a gift from God?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: What two pictures does the psalm use for children?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: How does calling children a "reward" change a stressful week?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: Where do you feel pressure to "perform" as a sibling or child—and how does grace answer that?

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: Direction over drama
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: Solomon — wisdom for the long road
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: Training is not a single lecture. It is direction repeated with patience.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: Train, way, old—this is a long picture, not a quick fix.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God honors faithful direction, even when the path wobbles.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: Pick one small habit to practice together for seven days (prayer, kindness, honesty). Keep it tiny.
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: Where are you tempted to use volume instead of direction?
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: What is one "way" our family is trying to walk—kindness, honesty, rest?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Circle one area to practice together this week; write it on the calendar.
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Lord, train us in Your way. Give us patience for the long arc, not just the loud moment. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw a path with two signposts: one says "train," one says "way."
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: What habit do we want to grow—not perfect, just truer?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: What does "train up" suggest about repetition?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: How is this verse misused—and how is it meant as mercy?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: What adult faith habit do you want to see modeled—honestly?

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: Do not discourage
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: Fathers, provoke not your children to anger, lest they be discouraged.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: Paul — to a church learning new family rhythms
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: Anger can be a habit in a home. God warns how it lands—in discouraged hearts.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: The warning is emotional: anger leads to discouragement.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God cares about a child's inner courage, not only outward compliance.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: Before bed once this week, bless each child with one specific encouragement.
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: Where does your tone land as discouragement—even when you are right?
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: What words help you try again after a mistake?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Share one encouragement each—no backhanded compliments.
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Jesus, guard our words. Let our home be a place where courage grows. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw a shield labeled "courage" blocking arrows labeled "harsh words."
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: When have words made you want to give up—and when have they helped you try again?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: What does Paul connect: anger and what outcome?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: How can parents correct without discouraging?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: What would it look like to "rebuild" after a harsh moment at home?

familyWorshipTrenches7.title: Joy in truth
familyWorshipTrenches7.text: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.
familyWorshipTrenches7.speaker: John — an elder writing with fatherly warmth
familyWorshipTrenches7.plain: The Christian life ends in truth—not performance, not applause. Parents ache for children to walk in it.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familySee: Joy tied to hearing truth lived out.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyUnderstand: God is pleased when children walk honestly with Christ—not when they merely look good.
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyLive: Finish the week with one honest family prayer: "Lord, help us walk in truth at home and away."
familyWorshipTrenches7.parentPrompt: Where do you need truth this week—confession, apology, courage?
familyWorshipTrenches7.kidQ: What is one true thing you want God to help you with?
familyWorshipTrenches7.familyTogether: Stand or hold hands. Thank God for one way you saw truth this week.
familyWorshipTrenches7.prayer: Lord, we want truth more than ease. Give us joy that matches walking with You. Amen.
familyWorshipTrenches7.drawPrompt: Draw footprints with the word "truth" on the path.
familyWorshipTrenches7.talkTogether: What does walking in truth look like in our house this week?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia58: What kind of joy is John talking about?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oia912: Why is "walk" a good word for daily faith?
familyWorshipTrenches7.oiaTeens: Where is truth costly for you right now—and how can we support you?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Shepherd care
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: David — before the valley
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: Belonging comes first: you are not alone with your feelings—the Shepherd is with you.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: What words describe God in this verse? (shepherd, want)
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: A shepherd leads and provides. God is not asking kids to be brave alone.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: At dinner, name one thing you are glad God takes care of for our family.
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Say one sentence: "We are not in charge of everything—and that is mercy."
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: What does a shepherd do for sheep?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyTogether: Whisper the first line of the psalm together once.
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: Lord, be our Shepherd. Teach us to trust Your care tonight. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw a sheep and a shepherd staff—or a simple path with someone walking beside you.
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: What is something we worry about that we could hand to God?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia58: Who is "my" shepherd—what does that word mean?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: What might "I shall not want" mean when we still feel sad sometimes?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: Where do you try to be your own shepherd—and what would it look like to let God lead?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Near the sad heart
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: David — after fear, after deliverance
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: God comes close when hearts feel cracked—not only when everyone is cheerful.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: What two kinds of people does God draw near to?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: God saves the humble, honest heart. He is not looking for a brave face.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: Each person shares one "small hard thing" from today—no fixing, just listening.
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Thank your kids for honest words, even if the tone was rough.
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: When you cry, do you think God moves closer or farther?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyTogether: Pray: "Thank You for being near when we are broken."
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: Lord, draw near to our broken places. Save us in the honest, quiet parts. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw a heart with a crack and a gentle hand beside it (God's nearness).
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: What helps you feel heard at home—and what makes you hide feelings?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia58: What does "nigh" mean in plain words?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: Why might God care about a contrite spirit?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: Where do you fake "fine"—and what would safety look like if you did not have to?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Strong help in trouble
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble.
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: The sons of Korah — when the ground shakes
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: Trouble is loud, but God is present—not far away.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: Name three words that describe God here (refuge, strength, help).
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: He is especially near when life feels shaky.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: Do a "pause and breathe" together for 30 seconds—then say one true thing about God.
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Name the trouble without solving it in one sentence.
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: What is a refuge—like a fort or a blanket fort?
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: God, be our refuge and strength. Be very present in our trouble today. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw a safe place (tent, house, or harbor) and label it "refuge."
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: What trouble feels loud right now—and what does God's nearness change?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: How is God's help different from just "feeling better"?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: Where do you feel trouble trying to name itself as "God is gone"—and what is true instead?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Light and courage
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: David — when fear was real
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: Fear names the room, but God names the light and the strength.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: What questions does the psalm ask twice?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: God is light and salvation—fear does not get the last word.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: Replace one worried "what if" tonight with: "The Lord is my light."
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Admit one fear in front of your kids, then point to God's care.
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: What scares you at school or at night—and who helps you?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyTogether: Whisper one fear, then read the first sentence of the verse slowly.
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: Lord, be our light and salvation. Turn down fear in our home. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw a small candle or sun and write "light" near it.
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: What fear shrinks when we remember God is light?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia58: What is God to David—light, salvation, strength?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: Why ask "whom shall I fear" twice?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: Which fear feels biggest—and how does this verse answer without pretending life is easy?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Under His shadow
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: A song of shelter
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: Staying close to God is like shade on a hot day—rest, not earning.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: Where does the person dwell—and what do they get?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: The Most High gives cover; we are invited to stay close.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: For two minutes, sit still together. No phones. Breathe. "Abide" means stay.
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Show kids what it looks like to rest in God—not rush.
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: What is a shadow good for when the sun is hot?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyTogether: Thank God for one way He has covered our family.
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: Most High, let us dwell in Your secret place. We want Your shadow, not our worry. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw a big tree or umbrella labeled "shadow" and stick figures underneath.
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: Where do we feel exposed—and how can we "stay close" to God this week?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia58: What is the secret place in simple words?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: What does it mean to abide—not visit once?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: What competes with abiding—noise, schedule, shame?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Help for the journey
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills, from whence cometh my help.
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: A pilgrim song
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: Help does not start inside our chest. It comes from the Lord.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: What does the psalmist do with his eyes?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: God is the source of help for the whole trip—not only the easy miles.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: Look out a window or at the sky; pray one sentence: "My help comes from You."
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Name one "hill" (stress) and lift your eyes past it in prayer.
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: Where do you look when you need help—phone, parent, God?
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: Lord, we lift our eyes. Our help comes from You—not from the size of the problem. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw hills and a small figure looking up.
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: What hill is our family staring at—and how can we look to God first?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia58: What action does the verse start with?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: Why might a traveler need this song?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: What do you try to fix alone that belongs in prayer?

psalmsComfortFamily7.title: Known and loved
psalmsComfortFamily7.text: O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.
psalmsComfortFamily7.speaker: David — before the wonder of being seen
psalmsComfortFamily7.plain: Nothing in you scares God away. He already knows—and stays.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familySee: What two things does God do—search and know.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyUnderstand: Being known is the start of comfort, not the end of hope.
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyLive: Each person finishes: "God knows me, and I can still talk to Him about __________."
psalmsComfortFamily7.parentPrompt: Tell your kids one way you are glad God knows you.
psalmsComfortFamily7.kidQ: Is it scary or good that God knows everything?
psalmsComfortFamily7.familyTogether: Thank God for loving what He knows.
psalmsComfortFamily7.prayer: Lord, You have searched us and known us. Thank You for love that stays. Amen.
psalmsComfortFamily7.drawPrompt: Draw a heart with the word "known" inside.
psalmsComfortFamily7.talkTogether: What part of life feels hidden—and how does God's knowing change that?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia58: What does "searched" mean—like a caring parent checking in?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oia912: Why is "known" good news on a hard day?
psalmsComfortFamily7.oiaTeens: Where do you feel misunderstood—and how does God's knowing help?

newBeliever14.title: We all miss the mark
newBeliever14.text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — leveling the ground before good news
newBeliever14.plain: No one earns their way to God by being "good enough." Sin is real—and universal.
newBeliever14.today: You do not have to pretend you have it together. God already knows the truth.
newBeliever14.action: Tell God one honest sentence: "I have missed the mark." No excuses.
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, I have sinned. I come to You without a mask. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Sin has a wage
newBeliever14.text: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — naming the cost and the gift in one breath
newBeliever14.plain: Death here is separation from God—spiritual and eternal. The gift is not wages you earned; it is given in Christ.
newBeliever14.today: Which side are you banking on—what you deserve, or what He gives?
newBeliever14.action: Write "gift" on a sticky note where you will see it. Let it remind you: eternal life is given.
newBeliever14.prayer: Father, thank You for the gift of life in Jesus—not wages I earned. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: While we were still sinners
newBeliever14.text: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — the heart of the gospel
newBeliever14.plain: Christ did not wait for you to clean up first. He died for you while you were still far off.
newBeliever14.today: What shame tells you that you are "too late"? Love got there first.
newBeliever14.action: Read this verse twice slowly. Let "while we were yet sinners" land.
newBeliever14.prayer: Jesus, You died for me while I was still a sinner. Thank You. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Believe and confess
newBeliever14.text: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved. For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — how faith becomes audible and real
newBeliever14.plain: Salvation is received by believing in the risen Christ and confessing Him as Lord—not by perfect feelings.
newBeliever14.today: Have you told God, out loud or in truth, that Jesus is your Lord?
newBeliever14.action: Say aloud: "Jesus is Lord. I believe God raised You from the dead."
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord Jesus, I believe in my heart and confess with my mouth. Save me. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Children of God
newBeliever14.text: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:
newBeliever14.speaker: John — right after the Word became flesh
newBeliever14.plain: Receive Him—not only information about Him. That is how people become God's children.
newBeliever14.today: Will you receive Him today—not as a story, but as your King?
newBeliever14.action: Pray: "I receive Jesus as He is—not as I imagined Him."
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, I receive You. Make me Yours. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Saved by grace through faith
newBeliever14.text: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — tearing up the scoreboard
newBeliever14.plain: You cannot brag your way in or shame your way out. Grace is a gift—not a paycheck.
newBeliever14.today: Where are you still trying to earn what is only given?
newBeliever14.action: Thank God for one thing you could never have earned—starting with salvation.
newBeliever14.prayer: Thank You for grace I did not earn. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: A new creation
newBeliever14.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — to people learning their new identity
newBeliever14.plain: In Christ, God is doing a new thing in you. It is not cosmetic—it is new creation.
newBeliever14.today: What "old thing" is God inviting you to leave with Him today?
newBeliever14.action: Write one word for something old you hand to Him. Fold the paper and pray over it.
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, I am in Christ. Make me new where I still feel stuck. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Abide in the vine
newBeliever14.text: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
newBeliever14.speaker: Jesus — the night before the cross
newBeliever14.plain: Stay connected to Him—daily, honestly. Fruit grows from abiding, not from striving alone.
newBeliever14.today: What does "abide" look like for you tomorrow morning for five quiet minutes?
newBeliever14.action: Set a reminder titled "Abide" for one still moment with Him.
newBeliever14.prayer: Jesus, I want to abide in You. Apart from You I can do nothing. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Pray to your Father
newBeliever14.text: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
newBeliever14.speaker: Jesus — teaching His disciples to pray
newBeliever14.plain: Prayer is not a performance. Secret honesty with God is the classroom of relationship.
newBeliever14.today: When will you shut the door—literally or figuratively—and pray simply today?
newBeliever14.action: Pray one minute with no requests—only "Father" and thanks.
newBeliever14.prayer: Father, I come to You in secret. Hear me. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: The Scriptures are enough
newBeliever14.text: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — charging Timothy to stay in the Book
newBeliever14.plain: The Bible is God-breathed and practical—not only for scholars, for formation.
newBeliever14.today: What one chapter or psalm will you read slowly before bed?
newBeliever14.action: Open the chapter reader or a printed Bible to one chapter and read without rushing.
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, teach me from Scripture. Furnish me for what You ask today. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Repent and be baptized
newBeliever14.text: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
newBeliever14.speaker: Peter — the first Christian sermon
newBeliever14.plain: Repent means turn toward God. Baptism is the public line in the sand—ask a trusted pastor what it means where you worship.
newBeliever14.today: Is there a next step—baptism or talking to a pastor—you have been postponing?
newBeliever14.action: Send one message or make one call to a church or mentor about your next step.
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, I repent and turn to You. Lead me in baptism and life with Your people. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Do not neglect gathering
newBeliever14.text: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
newBeliever14.speaker: The writer of Hebrews — to a tired church
newBeliever14.plain: Faith needs faces. Gathering is not optional luxury—it is how we stir one another up.
newBeliever14.today: Where will you assemble this week—a local church, a small group, a Bible study?
newBeliever14.action: Put one gathering on your calendar. Show up early enough to greet someone.
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, connect me with Your people. I need them; they need me. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: Christ lives in me
newBeliever14.text: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — the exchanged life
newBeliever14.plain: Your old self-reliant life was crucified with Christ. What lives now is His life in you—by faith.
newBeliever14.today: Where will you let "not I, but Christ" choose the next right step?
newBeliever14.action: Before one hard moment today, whisper: "Not I—but Christ in me."
newBeliever14.prayer: Jesus, live through me today. I trust You more than my old patterns. Amen.

newBeliever14.title: He finishes what He starts
newBeliever14.text: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
newBeliever14.speaker: Paul — thankful for the Philippians
newBeliever14.plain: God is not done with you. What He started in saving you, He will carry to completion.
newBeliever14.today: After fourteen days, what is one sign that His good work has begun in you?
newBeliever14.action: Write one sentence of thanks for this journey. Share it with God—or with one trusted person.
newBeliever14.prayer: Lord, You began this work in me. Perform it until Jesus comes. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: Name the noise
anxiousParent7.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
anxiousParent7.speaker: Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount
anxiousParent7.plain: Stop chasing the side things. Put God first and everything else lines up.
anxiousParent7.today: What worry about your children is filling your mind this morning?
anxiousParent7.action: Write one worry on paper, then set it face-down and open the Word instead.
anxiousParent7.prayer: Lord, I put You first today. Help me stop chasing what doesn't matter for my family. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: Cast your care
anxiousParent7.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.
anxiousParent7.speaker: Peter to scattered believers under pressure
anxiousParent7.plain: Your cares are not too heavy for Him. He cares for you and for them.
anxiousParent7.today: What specific fear for your child is weighing on you right now?
anxiousParent7.action: Speak the worry out loud once, then say "I cast this on You."
anxiousParent7.prayer: Father, I cast this care on You. You care for us. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: Be careful for nothing
anxiousParent7.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
anxiousParent7.speaker: Paul from prison
anxiousParent7.plain: Don't carry the weight alone. Pray it out with thanks. Peace comes.
anxiousParent7.today: What "everything" about parenting feels heaviest today?
anxiousParent7.action: Pray one specific request for your child out loud, then thank God for one thing about them.
anxiousParent7.prayer: Lord, I bring this to You with thanks. Guard my heart and mind. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: The Lord is my shepherd
anxiousParent7.text: The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want.
anxiousParent7.speaker: David
anxiousParent7.plain: You are not the only shepherd of your child. He leads both of you.
anxiousParent7.today: Where do you feel you are failing as a parent today?
anxiousParent7.action: Read this verse slowly. Then tell your child (or yourself) one way God is leading today.
anxiousParent7.prayer: Good Shepherd, I shall not want. Lead us both. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: Train up a child
anxiousParent7.text: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.
anxiousParent7.speaker: Solomon
anxiousParent7.plain: Your job is faithful training, not perfect control of the outcome.
anxiousParent7.today: What small habit are you trying to build in your home right now?
anxiousParent7.action: Do one small training step today (read one verse together, pray at bedtime, speak truth calmly).
anxiousParent7.prayer: Lord, help me train faithfully. The outcome is Yours. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: Peace I leave with you
anxiousParent7.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
anxiousParent7.speaker: Jesus to His disciples
anxiousParent7.plain: His peace is different. It can steady a parent's heart even when the house is loud.
anxiousParent7.today: What is making your heart troubled or afraid about parenting tonight?
anxiousParent7.action: Sit quietly for one minute and repeat "Let not your heart be troubled."
anxiousParent7.prayer: Jesus, leave Your peace with me. Do not let my heart be troubled. Amen.

anxiousParent7.title: My grace is sufficient
anxiousParent7.text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
anxiousParent7.speaker: The Lord to Paul
anxiousParent7.plain: You don't have to be strong enough. His grace is enough for today's parenting.
anxiousParent7.today: Where did you feel weak as a parent this week?
anxiousParent7.action: Name the weakness to God in one sentence. Then say "Your grace is sufficient for me."
anxiousParent7.prayer: Lord, my weakness shows Your strength. Your grace is sufficient. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: If any man be in Christ
identityInChrist7.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
identityInChrist7.speaker: Paul
identityInChrist7.plain: Your core identity is not your worst mistake or your best performance. In Christ, you are a new creation.
identityInChrist7.today: What old label are you still wearing that God has already replaced?
identityInChrist7.action: Write "new creature" on paper. Carry it for one day as a quiet reminder.
identityInChrist7.prayer: Lord, I am in Christ. Teach me to live from the new, not the old. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: Sons and heirs
identityInChrist7.text: For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ. There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.
identityInChrist7.speaker: Paul — unity under Christ
identityInChrist7.plain: Faith in Christ makes you God's child. The ground is level at the cross.
identityInChrist7.today: How does being God's child change how you talk to yourself today?
identityInChrist7.action: Start one sentence today with: "Because I am God's child, I can…"
identityInChrist7.prayer: Father, thank You that I am Your child by faith in Jesus. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: Power to become sons
identityInChrist7.text: But as many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, even to them that believe on his name:
identityInChrist7.speaker: John
identityInChrist7.plain: You are not an orphan in the universe. Reception of Jesus is how people become God's children.
identityInChrist7.today: Where do you feel like an outsider—and what changes if you are truly God's child?
identityInChrist7.action: Pray the Lord's Prayer slowly, pausing on "Our Father."
identityInChrist7.prayer: Our Father, I receive Your adoption. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: The Spirit bears witness
identityInChrist7.text: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God: And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.
identityInChrist7.speaker: Paul — to believers who groan and hope
identityInChrist7.plain: God's Spirit confirms what words cannot always feel: you belong to Him.
identityInChrist7.today: What fear says you are not really His? Let the Spirit's witness answer it.
identityInChrist7.action: Read verse 16 five times. Let "children of God" echo.
identityInChrist7.prayer: Spirit of God, bear witness with my spirit. I am Yours. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: Fellowcitizens and household
identityInChrist7.text: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
identityInChrist7.speaker: Paul — after describing peace between Jew and Gentile
identityInChrist7.plain: You are not a stranger at the door. You are family—with the saints, in God's household.
identityInChrist7.today: Where do you still feel like a foreigner in God's house?
identityInChrist7.action: Introduce yourself to one person at church or online Christian community this week.
identityInChrist7.prayer: Lord, I am of Your household. Help me live as family. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: A chosen generation
identityInChrist7.text: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
identityInChrist7.speaker: Peter — to exiles
identityInChrist7.plain: Chosen—not because you were shiny, but to declare the praises of the One who called you out of darkness.
identityInChrist7.today: What one praise can you "show forth" today—in word or deed?
identityInChrist7.action: Text or tell one person one true thing God has done for you.
identityInChrist7.prayer: Lord, You called me into light. Use me to show Your praise. Amen.

identityInChrist7.title: Hidden with Christ
identityInChrist7.text: If ye then be risen with Christ, seek those things which are above, where Christ sitteth on the right hand of God. Set your affection on things above, not on things on the earth. For ye are dead, and your life is hid with Christ in God.
identityInChrist7.speaker: Paul
identityInChrist7.plain: Your real life is hidden with Christ—safe in God—even when earth feels loud.
identityInChrist7.today: What earthly anxiety needs to lose its veto power over your identity?
identityInChrist7.action: Set affection above once an hour for three hours—one breath, one sentence of trust.
identityInChrist7.prayer: Lord, my life is hid with Christ in God. Anchor me there. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Enter with thanksgiving
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanksgiving is how you come in—not after you feel sorted.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What would it look like to enter prayer with thanks first?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Begin your next prayer with sixty seconds of thanks—no requests yet.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, I enter with thanksgiving. I bless Your name. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: His mercy endures
praiseThanksgiving30.text: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: David's song when the ark was brought back
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: His goodness is steady; His mercy outlasts your mood.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Name one way His mercy held you when you did not deserve it.
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Say this verse aloud before one meal today.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: O give thanks unto the LORD; His mercy endures. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: In everything give thanks
praiseThanksgiving30.text: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Not for evil—in everything, thanks is woven with trust that God is still God.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What hard "everything" can you thank Him in—not for—the situation, but for His nearness?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Pair one honest grief line with one thanks line in prayer.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Father, I give thanks in this day—not pretending, trusting You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Thanks with my whole heart
praiseThanksgiving30.text: I will praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: David
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Whole heart means undivided—not perfect, but aimed.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What divides your heart when you try to praise?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Write three marvellous works you have seen God do—ever.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, I praise You with my whole heart today. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Do all in His name
praiseThanksgiving30.text: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Ordinary words and deeds can carry thanks when Jesus is named over them.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What one conversation will you offer "in His name" today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Before speaking in one tense moment, breathe: "In Jesus' name—thanks."
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Jesus, let my words and deeds today give thanks through You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Sing with thanksgiving
praiseThanksgiving30.text: O come, let us sing unto the LORD: let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving, and make a joyful noise unto him with psalms.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Joyful noise is welcome—not only polished worship.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Hum or sing one line of praise in the car or kitchen.
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Clap once, laugh if you can, then pray one thanks.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Rock of my salvation, I come with thanksgiving. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Giving thanks always
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Giving thanks always for all things unto God and the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ;
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Always does not deny pain—it keeps thanks tied to the Father, in Jesus' name.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What can you thank Him for in the middle of a stress you did not choose?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Set a quiet alarm mid-day: one thanks, in Jesus' name.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Father, in Jesus' name, I thank You in all things today. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: This is the day
praiseThanksgiving30.text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Rejoice is a decision tethered to God making the day—not to ease.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What makes gladness possible even if circumstances are plain hard?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Say "we will rejoice" once before noon.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, this is Your day—I will rejoice and be glad in it. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Sing praises
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Sing unto the LORD, O ye saints of his, and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: David
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Holiness remembered turns memory into song.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What holy thing He did is worth remembering out loud?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Sing or speak one line of praise at the remembrance of His holiness.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Holy Lord, I give thanks at the remembrance of You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: O give thanks
praiseThanksgiving30.text: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: The book returns to this line after stories of trouble—thanks is the chorus.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What trouble are you walking through that still allows "He is good"?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Read Psalm 107:1-9 slowly.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: O give thanks—for You are good. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Sacrifice of thanksgiving
praiseThanksgiving30.text: But I will sacrifice unto thee with the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay that that I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Jonah — from the fish
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanks can be sacrifice—offered when feelings lag.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What vow or promise to God do you need to pay today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Offer thanks in one sentence when you least feel like it.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Salvation is of the LORD—I thank You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: He turned back giving thanks
praiseThanksgiving30.text: And one of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, and with a loud voice glorified God, And fell down on his face at his feet, giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Luke — ten healed, one returned
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Jesus notices the one who circles back with thanks.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What healing—big or small—needs a turned-back thank You today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Kneel in spirit or body for one minute of thanks.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Jesus, I turn back to thank You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: I thank my God
praiseThanksgiving30.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanks for people is thanks through Christ—faith is worth mentioning.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Whose faith can you thank God for—and maybe tell them?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Send one short encouragement text: "Thanking God for you."
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: I thank You, God, for Your people. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: With thanksgiving let requests
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Requests and thanks belong together—anxiety loses its monopoly.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What request will you frame with thanks today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Write one request, then three thanks, then pray both.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, I bring requests with thanksgiving. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Bless the Lord, O my soul
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul: and all that is within me, bless his holy name. Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: David
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Your soul needs directing toward blessing—not only comfort.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Which benefit have you forgotten this week?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: List five benefits from verse 2–5 on paper.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Bless the LORD, O my soul—all within me, bless His name. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: His mercy endures forever
praiseThanksgiving30.text: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: The refrain repeats because your heart forgets fast.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Say "for his mercy endureth for ever" each time doubt knocks.
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Read Psalm 136:1–9 and answer each line with "His mercy endureth for ever."
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Thank You—Your mercy endures forever. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Giving thanks unto the Father
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light:
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanks for qualified inheritance—light, not darkness.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What inheritance in light are you partaking today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Thank the Father aloud for making you meet for light.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Father, thank You for the inheritance of the saints in light. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Praise is comely
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: David
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Praise fits you—it is becoming for the upright.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What makes praise "comely" in your home or workplace today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Offer one upright praise—no irony, no performance.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, praise fits Your people—I rejoice in You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Before the gods
praiseThanksgiving30.text: I will praise thee with my whole heart: before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: David
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Praise goes public—before whatever claims allegiance in culture.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What "god" competes for praise—comfort, approval, control?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Sing or say one line of praise louder than you usually would.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: I praise You with my whole heart before every rival claim. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Fruit of our lips
praiseThanksgiving30.text: By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise to God continually, that is, the fruit of our lips giving thanks to his name.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The writer of Hebrews
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Praise is sacrifice sometimes—and fruit at the same time.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What continual praise can your lips offer while you work?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Whisper thanks to His name three times during one hour.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, receive the fruit of my lips. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: I thank thee, and praise thee
praiseThanksgiving30.text: I thank thee, and praise thee, O thou God of my fathers, who hast given me wisdom and might: for now hast thou made known unto me the thing we desired of thee: for thou hast now made known unto us the king's matter.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Daniel
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanks for wisdom and might—God makes the hidden known.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What "king's matter" do you need God to make clear?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Thank Him for wisdom before you see the full answer.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: God of my fathers, I thank and praise You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Great sacrifices, rejoicing
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Also that day they offered great sacrifices, and rejoiced: for God had made them rejoice with great joy: the wives also and the children rejoiced: so that the joy of Jerusalem was heard even afar off.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Nehemiah
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Joy can be loud—community thanks carries.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Who in your household can rejoice with you today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Share one thanks at the table or on the couch—include kids if you can.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, let our joy in You be heard—starting at home. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Thanks be unto God
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: The gift is Christ—language stalls. Thanks does not.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Sit in silence one minute: thanks for the unspeakable gift.
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Write "unspeakable gift" on a card; glance at it twice today.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Thanks be unto God for Jesus. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Good to give thanks
praiseThanksgiving30.text: It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD, and to sing praises unto thy name, O most High:
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Good—not trendy. Thanks is fitting.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Morning or night—which fits a song of praise for you today?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Name the time you will thank Him once—then do it.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Most High, it is good to give thanks to You. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Sing with thanksgiving
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Sing unto the LORD with thanksgiving; sing praise upon the harp unto our God:
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Sing and thanks pair—voice and instrument optional, heart required.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What song of praise can you offer—even quietly?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Play a hymn or psalm tune and hum along.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, I sing with thanksgiving. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: We give thee thanks
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Saying, We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Heavenly voices in John's vision
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: God reigns—thanks follows His power exercised rightly.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What does His reign change about your worry list?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: End one worry sentence with "Thou hast reigned."
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: O Lord God Almighty, we give You thanks. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Thank Christ Jesus our Lord
praiseThanksgiving30.text: And I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who hath enabled me, for that he counted me faithful, putting me into the ministry;
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: Paul
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanks for enablement and calling—even when you feel unqualified.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What has Christ enabled you to do that you could not alone?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Thank Him for one enabling grace—speech, patience, courage.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Christ Jesus my Lord, I thank You for enabling me. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Sacrifice of thanksgiving
praiseThanksgiving30.text: I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, and will call upon the name of the LORD.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Thanks costs something—time, pride, agenda.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What sacrifice of thanks will you offer before you call for more help?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Thank before you ask in your next prayer.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Lord, I offer thanksgiving and call on Your name. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Hope thou in God
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope thou in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The sons of Korah
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: Honest ache and future praise can share the same breath.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: Where is your soul cast down—and can you hope in God there?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Speak verse 11 to yourself in a mirror or window once.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: I shall yet praise Him—my health and my God. Amen.

praiseThanksgiving30.title: Everything that hath breath
praiseThanksgiving30.text: Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.
praiseThanksgiving30.speaker: The psalmist
praiseThanksgiving30.plain: If you have breath, you have a reason—thirty days built on that.
praiseThanksgiving30.today: What changed in how you thank Him over these thirty days?
praiseThanksgiving30.action: Write one line: "Because of these thirty days, I now…" Thank Him aloud.
praiseThanksgiving30.prayer: Let everything that has breath praise You. Praise ye the LORD. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Be strong in the Lord
armorGod7.text: Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.
armorGod7.speaker: Paul — closing the letter with battle orders
armorGod7.plain: Your strength is not self-made; it is the Lord's. The devil has schemes—God gives armor.
armorGod7.today: Where have you been fighting in your own strength instead of His?
armorGod7.action: Say once: "Strong in the Lord—not in me." Then ask Him for one piece of His strength for today.
armorGod7.prayer: Lord, I am strong in You and in Your might. Help me stand. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Not flesh and blood
armorGod7.text: For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.
armorGod7.speaker: Paul
armorGod7.plain: People are not the final enemy. There is a dark hierarchy behind the noise—pray accordingly.
armorGod7.today: Who are you tempted to treat as the enemy that is really a fellow wrestler in the dust?
armorGod7.action: Pray for one hard person by name—blessing, not cursing.
armorGod7.prayer: Father, I wrestle not against flesh and blood. Give me clear eyes. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Take unto you the armour
armorGod7.text: Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand.
armorGod7.speaker: Paul
armorGod7.plain: Take it—active. Evil days come; after everything, still stand.
armorGod7.today: What would "having done all, to stand" look like in your week?
armorGod7.action: Name one evil day habit you will refuse today (scroll, rumination, isolation).
armorGod7.prayer: God, I take Your whole armour. I will stand. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Truth and righteousness
armorGod7.text: Stand therefore, having your loins girt about with truth, and having on the breastplate of righteousness;
armorGod7.speaker: Paul
armorGod7.plain: Truth holds you together; righteousness guards the heart.
armorGod7.today: Where is a half-truth or a hidden story weakening you?
armorGod7.action: Tell one true thing—to God in prayer, or to one safe person.
armorGod7.prayer: Gird me with truth; guard my heart with righteousness. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Feet and faith
armorGod7.text: And your feet shod with the preparation of the gospel of peace; Above all, taking the shield of faith, wherewith ye shall be able to quench all the fiery darts of the wicked.
armorGod7.speaker: Paul
armorGod7.plain: Peace is how you move; faith turns aside what hell throws.
armorGod7.today: What fiery dart hit you this week—shame, fear, lust, accusation?
armorGod7.action: Lift the shield once: "I believe what God says about this."
armorGod7.prayer: Lord, shod my feet with peace; I take the shield of faith. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Helmet and sword
armorGod7.text: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God:
armorGod7.speaker: Paul
armorGod7.plain: Salvation guards your mind; Scripture is your offensive blade—not opinion, not rumor.
armorGod7.today: What thought needs the helmet today?
armorGod7.action: Speak one verse aloud—even one sentence of KJV you know.
armorGod7.prayer: Helmet of salvation on; Your word in my mouth. Amen.

armorGod7.title: Praying always
armorGod7.text: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
armorGod7.speaker: Paul
armorGod7.plain: The armor fits a praying saint—watching, persevering, carrying others.
armorGod7.today: Which saint needs your supplication today?
armorGod7.action: Pray sixty seconds for one believer by name.
armorGod7.prayer: Spirit, help me pray always and watch. I intercede for Your people. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: Poor in spirit
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: Jesus begins with the ones who feel empty inside. When we admit we don't have it all together, He opens the door to His kingdom. You don't need to be strong or impressive—just honest. That's where the blessing starts.
beatitudes9.today: Where do you feel weak or empty before God today?
beatitudes9.action: Quietly tell God one area where you feel weak or empty. Let Him meet you there.
beatitudes9.prayer: Lord, I come to You poor in spirit. Fill me with Your kingdom. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: They that mourn
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: Sadness is not a sign of weakness. Jesus sees every tear and every heavy heart. When we bring our sorrow to Him, He draws near with comfort that the world cannot give.
beatitudes9.today: What is making your heart heavy today?
beatitudes9.action: Name one thing that makes your heart heavy today, then sit quietly with Jesus for two minutes.
beatitudes9.prayer: Jesus, You see my sadness. Comfort me with Your gentle presence. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: The meek
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: Meekness is quiet strength under God's control—not pushing others down, but choosing gentleness. The world says the loudest win; Jesus says the gentle inherit everything.
beatitudes9.today: Where are you tempted to be sharp when softness would honor Him?
beatitudes9.action: Choose one moment today to respond with softness instead of sharpness.
beatitudes9.prayer: Lord, make me meek like You. Teach my heart to rest in Your control. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: Hunger and thirst
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: A deep longing to live rightly is a holy hunger. Jesus promises that those who want to please God will never stay empty—He fills them.
beatitudes9.today: What do you long for God to make right in you or around you?
beatitudes9.action: Ask God for one small way you can choose righteousness today.
beatitudes9.prayer: Father, give me a hunger for what is right. Fill me with Yourself. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: The merciful
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: Mercy is love when someone doesn't deserve it. When we show mercy, we open our own hearts to receive the mercy God is always ready to give.
beatitudes9.today: Who needs mercy from you—and who has shown you mercy lately?
beatitudes9.action: Offer one quiet act of kindness or forgiveness today—no one else needs to know.
beatitudes9.prayer: Lord, make me merciful as You are merciful to me. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: Pure in heart
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: A pure heart is one that wants God more than anything else. Even when our thoughts wander, Jesus gently cleanses and draws us close so we can see Him more clearly.
beatitudes9.today: What is pulling your heart away from wanting Him first?
beatitudes9.action: Take one minute to pray, "Create in me a clean heart," and let God quiet your mind.
beatitudes9.prayer: Jesus, purify my heart so I may see You today. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: The peacemakers
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: Peacemakers don't just avoid fights—they bring calm into storms. When we choose peace, we look most like our Father.
beatitudes9.today: Where could you bring calm instead of adding heat?
beatitudes9.action: Bring peace to one small moment today—a soft word, a listening ear, or a quiet prayer.
beatitudes9.prayer: Father, make me a peacemaker so others see Your heart in me. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: Persecuted for righteousness
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness' sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
beatitudes9.plain: Sometimes doing right costs us something. Jesus says even then we are blessed—the kingdom belongs to those who stand with Him.
beatitudes9.today: Where does standing for truth feel costly today?
beatitudes9.action: If you face a hard choice today, remember the kingdom is already yours.
beatitudes9.prayer: Lord, when standing for You is hard, remind me the kingdom is mine. Amen.

beatitudes9.title: Rejoice and be glad
beatitudes9.text: Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.
beatitudes9.speaker: Jesus on the mount
