sowerKids7.title: Seed on the hard path
sowerKids7.text: When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.
sowerKids7.speaker: Jesus explaining the parable
sowerKids7.plain: Some seed lands on a hard path where feet walk. It cannot sink in, and the enemy snatches it away like a hungry bird.
sowerKids7.today: When do Bible words bounce away before they stick?
sowerKids7.action: Whisper, "Jesus, soften my heart," before school or bedtime.
sowerKids7.prayer: Lord, soften my heart so Your Word can stay. Amen.

sowerKids7.title: Seed on rocky ground
sowerKids7.text: But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it; Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended.
sowerKids7.speaker: Jesus explaining the parable
sowerKids7.plain: Some seed lands on shallow rocks. A plant pops up fast and happy, but it has no deep roots. When trouble comes, it dries up.
sowerKids7.today: What kind of day makes faith feel wobbly?
sowerKids7.action: Tell Jesus you want roots that go deep when things get hard.
sowerKids7.prayer: Jesus, give me deep roots so I can stand strong. Amen.

sowerKids7.title: Seed in thorny weeds
sowerKids7.text: He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful.
sowerKids7.speaker: Jesus explaining the parable
sowerKids7.plain: Some seed lands where weeds grow. Worries and wanting too much stuff crowd out God's Word—like thorns choking a plant.
sowerKids7.today: What worry or "I want" thought got loud today?
sowerKids7.action: Give one worry or noisy want to God in a quiet sentence.
sowerKids7.prayer: Father, clear the thorns so Your Word can grow in me. Amen.

sowerKids7.title: Good soil
sowerKids7.text: But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
sowerKids7.speaker: Jesus explaining the parable
sowerKids7.plain: Some seed lands in soft, good dirt. It listens, understands, and grows fruit—lots more than what was planted.
sowerKids7.today: How has God's Word helped you do something kind?
sowerKids7.action: Thank Jesus out loud for one small way His Word is growing in you.
sowerKids7.prayer: Lord, make my heart good soil that grows fruit for You. Amen.

sowerKids7.title: The farmer keeps sowing
sowerKids7.text: And he spake many things unto them in parables, saying, Behold, a sower went forth to sow;
sowerKids7.speaker: Jesus by the sea
sowerKids7.plain: The farmer keeps throwing seed—even toward ground that looks so-so. Jesus keeps sharing His Word with love and patience. He does not give up on you.
sowerKids7.today: When did someone give you another chance?
sowerKids7.action: Remember today that God is patient and kind to you.
sowerKids7.prayer: Thank You, Jesus, for never running out of seed for my heart. Amen.

sowerKids7.title: Ears to hear
sowerKids7.text: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
sowerKids7.speaker: Jesus closing the parable
sowerKids7.plain: Jesus ends with a gentle hush: "Who hath ears to hear, let him hear." He invites us to ask God to make our hearts ready soil.
sowerKids7.today: What kind of heart-soil feels most like yours today?
sowerKids7.action: Ask God to help your heart listen and grow—one quiet question is enough.
sowerKids7.prayer: Jesus, help my heart hear You and grow good fruit. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 1: Be still
summerSeeds8.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
summerSeeds8.speaker: The psalmist
summerSeeds8.plain: Summer is a good time to slow down and remember God is in control—not rushed, not noisy, just true.
summerSeeds8.today: What usually fills the quiet when you could be still with Him?
summerSeeds8.action: Sit outside or by a window for about two minutes and just listen.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Lord, help me be still and know You. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 2: God cares for the birds
summerSeeds8.text: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
summerSeeds8.speaker: Jesus on the mount
summerSeeds8.plain: Jesus reminds us that God takes care of the birds. He will take care of us too—we matter more to our Father than they do.
summerSeeds8.today: What worry about "enough" can you hand to Him today?
summerSeeds8.action: Watch birds or notice something God made outside; thank Him for His care.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Thank You for taking care of me, Father. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 3: Light burdens
summerSeeds8.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
summerSeeds8.speaker: Jesus
summerSeeds8.plain: Jesus invites us to bring heavy feelings to Him and find rest—His yoke is kind; His burden does not crush.
summerSeeds8.today: What feels heavy in your chest or thoughts right now?
summerSeeds8.action: Tell Jesus one thing that feels heavy—in a whisper is enough.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Jesus, I give You my heavy things. Give me Your rest. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 4: Growing quietly
summerSeeds8.text: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.
summerSeeds8.speaker: Jesus
summerSeeds8.plain: Growth often happens quietly, like seed in the soil—God is working even when we cannot see it yet.
summerSeeds8.today: Where do you wish you could see growth faster—and can you trust God's quiet timing?
summerSeeds8.action: Water a plant or draw a small sprout; thank God for quiet growth.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Help me grow quietly in You, Lord. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 5: Joy in simple things
summerSeeds8.text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.
summerSeeds8.speaker: The psalmist
summerSeeds8.plain: Every day is a gift from the Lord—even an ordinary summer day. We can rejoice and be glad in it.
summerSeeds8.today: What simple gift has today already held?
summerSeeds8.action: Name one simple thing you enjoyed today and thank God for it.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Thank You for this day. Help me rejoice in it. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 6: Trust like a child
summerSeeds8.text: And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
summerSeeds8.speaker: Jesus
summerSeeds8.plain: Jesus loves childlike trust—simple, open, and honest before God. You do not have to pretend you have it all figured out.
summerSeeds8.today: Where could you come to God more simply today?
summerSeeds8.action: Do one small playful or gentle thing and remember: He loves you.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Help me trust You like a child, Jesus. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 7: End with praise
summerSeeds8.text: Let every thing that hath breath praise the LORD. Praise ye the LORD.
summerSeeds8.speaker: The psalmist
summerSeeds8.plain: Summer evenings are a sweet time to end the day with simple praise—if you have breath, you have a reason to praise Him.
summerSeeds8.today: What from this week do you want to thank God for out loud?
summerSeeds8.action: List or whisper three things you praise God for this week.
summerSeeds8.prayer: I praise You, Lord, for this summer. Amen.

summerSeeds8.title: Summer Seeds — Week 8: Looking forward
summerSeeds8.text: Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ:
summerSeeds8.speaker: Paul
summerSeeds8.plain: God is still working in you—even through summer. What He started, He will carry on; you are not alone in the growing.
summerSeeds8.today: What good work do you think God has begun in you lately?
summerSeeds8.action: Thank God for one way He has been working in your life this summer.
summerSeeds8.prayer: Thank You that You finish what You start in me. Amen.

longIllness7.title: Outward and inward
longIllness7.text: For which cause we faint not; but though our outward man perish, yet the inward man is renewed day by day.
longIllness7.speaker: Paul
longIllness7.plain: The outside can weaken while the inside is renewed—both can be true.
longIllness7.today: Where do you feel the outward perishing loudest?
longIllness7.action: Thank God for one inward renewal you have seen—even patience you did not have last year.
longIllness7.prayer: Renew the inward while the outward struggles; I faint not. Amen.

longIllness7.title: Strength of my heart
longIllness7.text: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.
longIllness7.speaker: Asaph
longIllness7.plain: Failure of flesh is not the last line—God remains strength and portion.
longIllness7.today: When flesh and heart fail, where do you turn first—scroll, anger, or Him?
longIllness7.action: Speak the second half of the verse aloud twice today.
longIllness7.prayer: Strength of my heart and my portion—be enough today. Amen.

longIllness7.title: Mount up as eagles
longIllness7.text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
longIllness7.speaker: Isaiah
longIllness7.plain: Waiting on God is active trust—not limp passivity.
longIllness7.today: What does waiting look like for you this week—complaint or trust?
longIllness7.action: Sit by a window or outside five minutes; breathe; say "I wait on You."
longIllness7.prayer: I wait on You—renew strength I cannot manufacture. Amen.

longIllness7.title: Brokenhearted
longIllness7.text: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.
longIllness7.speaker: David
longIllness7.plain: Long illness breaks hearts; God draws near there—not only to the cheerful.
longIllness7.today: Is your spirit contrite before Him or only angry?
longIllness7.action: Tell Him one honest sentence about the ache.
longIllness7.prayer: You are near the brokenhearted—be near me. Amen.

longIllness7.title: New every morning
longIllness7.text: It is of the LORD'S mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
longIllness7.speaker: Jeremiah
longIllness7.plain: Mercy is daily ration—not one grant for the whole trial.
longIllness7.today: What mercy showed up this morning you almost missed?
longIllness7.action: Before sleep, name one mercy from today.
longIllness7.prayer: Great is Your faithfulness—new mercy tomorrow. Amen.

longIllness7.title: Grace sufficient
longIllness7.text: And he said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
longIllness7.speaker: The Lord to Paul
longIllness7.plain: Weakness is not the obstacle to grace—it is where strength completes its work.
longIllness7.today: What weakness are you hiding that He wants to meet with grace?
longIllness7.action: Pray "Your grace is sufficient" before one hard task.
longIllness7.prayer: Your strength in my weakness—thank You. Amen.

longIllness7.title: Not worthy to be compared
longIllness7.text: For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us.
longIllness7.speaker: Paul
longIllness7.plain: This does not erase pain—it sets pain beside a glory weightier than years of ache.
longIllness7.today: Can you hold both: this hurts, and glory is coming?
longIllness7.action: Read Romans 8:18-23 once; underline one hope phrase.
longIllness7.prayer: Hold me in present sufferings and coming glory. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: God is with you
backToSchoolCourage7.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: The LORD to Joshua
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: A new school year can feel big; God still says be strong—He goes with you in every hallway and lesson.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: Where does your stomach tighten when you think about school?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: Whisper once before you start the day: "The Lord my God is with me today."
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Lord, be with me today. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: Strength for the day
backToSchoolCourage7.text: But they that wait upon the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: Isaiah
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: When you feel tired or nervous, God gives fresh strength to those who wait on Him—not rush ahead without Him.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: What drains you before the day is half over?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: Take three slow breaths; thank God for strength you did not manufacture yourself.
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Lord, renew my strength today. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: Wisdom for learning
backToSchoolCourage7.text: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: James
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: God loves to give wisdom when we ask—no scolding for not knowing.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: Which subject or test has you stuck or worried?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: Before that class or study block, quietly ask God for wisdom—one honest sentence.
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Father, give me wisdom today. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: Kindness at school
backToSchoolCourage7.text: And be ye kind one to another, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ's sake hath forgiven you.
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: Paul
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: Jesus calls us to be kind and tenderhearted—even when others are not.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: Who might need patience from you today?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: Do one small kind thing for someone at school or on the ride home.
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Help me be kind like You, Jesus. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: Peace in the noise
backToSchoolCourage7.text: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: Jesus
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: His peace is not the world's noise-control—it is a quiet gift that can stay when the day feels loud.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: What usually steals your calm between classes or at home?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: When stress spikes, whisper: "Jesus, Your peace is mine."
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Jesus, give me Your peace today. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: Courage to stand
backToSchoolCourage7.text: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? the LORD is the strength of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: David
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: When doing the right thing feels scary, God is light and courage—not you muscling alone.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: What right thing have you been putting off because it feels risky?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: Choose one right thing today, even if your hands shake a little.
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Lord, be my light and my courage. Amen.

backToSchoolCourage7.title: Thoughts of peace
backToSchoolCourage7.text: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the LORD, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
backToSchoolCourage7.speaker: The LORD to exiles in Babylon
backToSchoolCourage7.plain: God spoke to a people far from home: His intent toward them was peace and a future—not harm. He is still trustworthy with your year.
backToSchoolCourage7.today: What part of this school year do you need to leave in His hands?
backToSchoolCourage7.action: Thank God aloud for one good thing He has already done in your life this year.
backToSchoolCourage7.prayer: Thank You for Your good thoughts toward me. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: Enter with thanks
harvestGratitude7.text: Enter into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise: be thankful unto him, and bless his name.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: The psalmist
harvestGratitude7.plain: Thanksgiving is how we draw near—not a holiday decoration, but the door.
harvestGratitude7.today: What is one true thank-you you can offer God today?
harvestGratitude7.action: Before a meal, say one specific thanks out loud.
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Thank You, Lord, for every good gift. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: His mercy endures
harvestGratitude7.text: O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good; for his mercy endureth for ever.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: David's song of thanks
harvestGratitude7.plain: God's mercy does not wear out; that is worth repeating.
harvestGratitude7.today: Where have you seen His mercy lately?
harvestGratitude7.action: Write or say three words: "His mercy endures."
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Lord, You are good. Your mercy lasts forever. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: Give thanks for kindness
harvestGratitude7.text: O give thanks unto the LORD, for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: The psalmist
harvestGratitude7.plain: Same heartbeat: the Lord is good; His mercy never ends.
harvestGratitude7.today: Who needs to hear "thank you" from you today?
harvestGratitude7.action: Thank one person for something small they did.
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Father, thank You for people who show kindness. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: Every good gift
harvestGratitude7.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: James
harvestGratitude7.plain: Good things trace back to God—the Father who does not shift like shadows.
harvestGratitude7.today: What good gift from God do you often forget?
harvestGratitude7.action: Name one "good gift" aloud before bed.
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Thank You for good gifts, Father of lights. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: Do all in His name
harvestGratitude7.text: And whatsoever ye do in word or deed, do all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God and the Father by him.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: Paul
harvestGratitude7.plain: Homework, chores, words to friends—can be offered in Jesus' name with thanks.
harvestGratitude7.today: What ordinary task can you do for Him today?
harvestGratitude7.action: Before one task, whisper: "For Jesus—thank You, Father."
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Jesus, help me live and speak in Your name with thanks. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: I will praise
harvestGratitude7.text: I will praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart; I will shew forth all thy marvellous works.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: David
harvestGratitude7.plain: Whole-heart praise is honesty about what God has done—not a performance.
harvestGratitude7.today: What marvellous work of God could you tell someone about?
harvestGratitude7.action: Share one way God helped you with a family member or friend.
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Lord, I praise You with my whole heart. Amen.

harvestGratitude7.title: In every thing give thanks
harvestGratitude7.text: In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
harvestGratitude7.speaker: Paul
harvestGratitude7.plain: Thanks is not pretending hard things are easy—it is trusting God even inside them.
harvestGratitude7.today: What hard thing can you bring to God with a small "thank You" for His presence?
harvestGratitude7.action: Offer one short thanks-prayer about a difficult situation.
harvestGratitude7.prayer: Father, teach me to give thanks in every season. Amen.

adventQuiet7.title: A child is born
adventQuiet7.text: For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.
adventQuiet7.speaker: Isaiah
adventQuiet7.plain: God's people waited; the promise has names—Wonderful, Prince of Peace.
adventQuiet7.today: What are you waiting for God to do this season?
adventQuiet7.action: Light a candle or draw a simple star; whisper "Prince of Peace."
adventQuiet7.prayer: Lord, help me wait quietly for You. Amen.

adventQuiet7.title: God with us
adventQuiet7.text: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
adventQuiet7.speaker: Isaiah
adventQuiet7.plain: Immanuel—God with us—spoken long before Bethlehem.
adventQuiet7.today: Where do you need to remember God is with you?

adventQuiet7.title: Little Bethlehem
adventQuiet7.text: But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.
adventQuiet7.speaker: Micah
adventQuiet7.plain: The King comes from a small place—God loves humble beginnings.
adventQuiet7.today: What small thing in your life might God be using?
adventQuiet7.action: Find Bethlehem on a map or globe; thank God for small places.
adventQuiet7.prayer: Lord, You choose humble places. Use my heart too. Amen.

adventQuiet7.title: Mary's song
adventQuiet7.text: And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
adventQuiet7.speaker: Mary
adventQuiet7.plain: Mary's soul makes God bigger in her eyes—not pride, but wonder.
adventQuiet7.today: What about God makes your spirit rejoice?
adventQuiet7.action: Say slowly: "My soul magnifies the Lord."
adventQuiet7.prayer: My soul magnifies You, Lord. Amen.

adventQuiet7.title: He shall save
adventQuiet7.text: And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.
adventQuiet7.speaker: The angel to Joseph
adventQuiet7.plain: His name means salvation—He came to save, not to scold.
adventQuiet7.today: What does being saved by Jesus mean to you today?
adventQuiet7.action: Whisper the name "Jesus" three times with thanks.
adventQuiet7.prayer: Jesus, thank You for coming to save. Amen.

adventQuiet7.title: Good tidings
adventQuiet7.text: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people. For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
adventQuiet7.speaker: The angel to shepherds
adventQuiet7.plain: Shepherds first heard it: a Saviour, Christ the Lord—for all people.
adventQuiet7.today: Who needs to hear that God brings good tidings, not only noise?
adventQuiet7.action: Read this verse aloud with family or alone by a window.
adventQuiet7.prayer: Lord, great joy—You are Christ the Lord. Amen.

adventQuiet7.title: The Word made flesh
adventQuiet7.text: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
adventQuiet7.speaker: John
adventQuiet7.plain: God's Word became a person we could know—grace and truth together.
adventQuiet7.today: How have you seen Jesus' grace and truth this week?
adventQuiet7.action: Thank God for one way Jesus has been real to you—not abstract.
adventQuiet7.prayer: Thank You for dwelling among us, full of grace and truth. Amen.

gentleYearReset5.title: New every morning
gentleYearReset5.text: It is of the LORD's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.
gentleYearReset5.speaker: Jeremiah
gentleYearReset5.plain: A new calendar does not restart the soul—God's mercies do, fresh each morning.
gentleYearReset5.today: What would it mean to receive today as mercy, not a test?
gentleYearReset5.action: Before sleep, whisper: "Great is Thy faithfulness."
gentleYearReset5.prayer: Father, Your compassions are new this morning. Amen.

gentleYearReset5.title: Number our days
gentleYearReset5.text: So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.
gentleYearReset5.speaker: Moses
gentleYearReset5.plain: Wisdom begins when we remember days are counted—and given by God.
gentleYearReset5.today: What wise choice does your heart need today?
gentleYearReset5.action: Write today's date and one line: "I want wisdom for this day."
gentleYearReset5.prayer: Teach me to number my days, Lord. Amen.

gentleYearReset5.title: A time for everything
gentleYearReset5.text: To every thing there is a season, and a time to every purpose under the heaven:
gentleYearReset5.speaker: The Preacher
gentleYearReset5.plain: Not every week feels the same—and that is by design under heaven.
gentleYearReset5.today: What season are you in—rest, work, grief, joy?
gentleYearReset5.action: Name your season aloud to God in one honest phrase.
gentleYearReset5.prayer: Lord, You hold my seasons. I trust Your timing. Amen.

gentleYearReset5.title: New creature
gentleYearReset5.text: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
gentleYearReset5.speaker: Paul
gentleYearReset5.plain: Christ makes new—not a patch on the old you alone.
gentleYearReset5.today: What old habit or label is Jesus inviting you to leave with Him?
gentleYearReset5.action: Thank God for one new thing He has already done in you.
gentleYearReset5.prayer: Lord, make me new in Christ. Amen.

gentleYearReset5.title: Press forward
gentleYearReset5.text: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forth unto those things which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
gentleYearReset5.speaker: Paul
gentleYearReset5.plain: Forward in Christ is not pretending the past did not happen—it is not letting yesterday own today.
gentleYearReset5.today: What is behind that you need to leave with God?
gentleYearReset5.action: Stretch your hands forward once; picture reaching toward Christ.
gentleYearReset5.prayer: Jesus, I press toward You. Amen.

summerStillness5.title: Be still
summerStillness5.text: Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.
summerStillness5.speaker: The psalmist
summerStillness5.plain: Summer noise fades when we pause long enough to remember who God is.
summerStillness5.today: What usually fills the silence when you could be still?
summerStillness5.action: Sit outside or by a window for two minutes—listen; then say "You are God."
summerStillness5.prayer: Lord, I am still. You are God. Amen.

summerStillness5.title: Come and rest
summerStillness5.text: Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.
summerStillness5.speaker: Jesus
summerStillness5.plain: Jesus invites tired people—not only the "put together" ones.
summerStillness5.today: What makes you feel heavy laden this summer?
summerStillness5.action: Tell Jesus one heavy thing in a short sentence.
summerStillness5.prayer: Jesus, I come to You for rest. Amen.

summerStillness5.title: Still waters
summerStillness5.text: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
summerStillness5.speaker: David
summerStillness5.plain: The Shepherd leads beside quiet water—not only through valleys.
summerStillness5.today: Where could you slow down to lie down with Him today?
summerStillness5.action: Drink a glass of water slowly; thank God for daily care.
summerStillness5.prayer: Good Shepherd, lead me beside still waters. Amen.

summerStillness5.title: Come apart awhile
summerStillness5.text: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
summerStillness5.speaker: Jesus to His disciples
summerStillness5.plain: Even His friends needed rest when crowds never stopped.
summerStillness5.today: When did you last have leisure to eat or breathe without rushing?
summerStillness5.action: Block twenty minutes today for quiet—no feed, just rest.
summerStillness5.prayer: Lord, help me rest awhile with You. Amen.

summerStillness5.title: Quietness and confidence
summerStillness5.text: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not:
summerStillness5.speaker: God through Isaiah
summerStillness5.plain: Strength can be quiet trust—not only loud effort.
summerStillness5.today: Where are you trying to be strong without resting in God?
summerStillness5.action: Read this verse twice—pause on "quietness and confidence."
summerStillness5.prayer: Father, be my strength in quietness. Amen.
